categories.name: ERP & Business Management
categories.description: Compare integrated finance and operations systems for US companies with complex orders, inventory, projects or multiple entities.
categories.buyerQuestion: Which operational bottlenecks justify a shared ERP, and which modules must be live on day one?
categories.intro: ERP is a process change as much as a software purchase. A useful shortlist starts with the operational handoffs that currently fail: sales orders retyped into finance, stock that does not match the warehouse, project costs assembled in spreadsheets or subsidiary balances consolidated manually. Compare systems against those tasks and the people responsible for them. A finance-led platform and an inventory-led ERP can both be strong choices for different businesses. A larger feature list does not establish a better fit. Your first release needs a credible implementation scope, reliable data and clear ownership of exceptions.

criteria.label: Financial management
criteria.why: The system must support the core transaction and close workflows.

criteria.label: Inventory, orders & operations
criteria.why: Match operational modules to the actual business, not a generic suite list.

criteria.label: Entities & consolidation
criteria.why: Entity structure and currency needs can materially change architecture and price.

criteria.label: Integration & configuration
criteria.why: Extensions, APIs and supported integrations determine maintainability.

criteria.label: Embedded AI & governance
criteria.why: Verify deployed task-level AI, permissions, availability and incremental cost.

criteria.label: Operational detail
criteria.why: Specific workflow, integration and control checks beyond the established rubric.

buyingAdvice.title: Build a script around your hardest normal day
buyingAdvice.body: Write a scenario that includes a normal order and the exceptions that repeatedly cost time: a partial shipment, returned item, price change, substituted supplier, intercompany transaction or project cost correction. Require vendors and implementation partners to show the end-to-end process in the proposed edition. Mark each step as standard, configured, extended or outside scope. That distinction matters more than a broad promise that the platform can do it. Include warehouse, operations and finance staff in the evaluation so an improvement for one department does not create manual work for another.

buyingAdvice.title: Treat the implementation proposal as part of the product
buyingAdvice.body: Ask for named deliverables covering data migration, integrations, role design, testing, training, cutover and post-launch support. Specify which historical records will move and which will remain in a searchable archive. Require the partner to explain how customizations survive upgrades and who resolves an integration failure after go-live. A license quote without implementation assumptions cannot support a budget. Agree on acceptance tests and business owners before signing. For a phased rollout, define what the first phase excludes and how those exclusions will be handled without creating a permanent parallel spreadsheet system.

buyingAdvice.title: Price the next stage of growth
buyingAdvice.body: Compare licensing under the staffing, transaction volume and company structure you expect in two years, as well as today's baseline. Per-user, consumption-based and module-based models scale differently. Ask about read-only users, external users, additional companies, sandbox environments, API capacity and advanced planning. For AI, separate an included assistant from metered agents, third-party model costs or newly announced capabilities. Demonstrate approval boundaries with a low-privilege test user. A natural-language answer should not become an excuse to bypass controls over purchasing, inventory adjustments or financial posting.

costDrivers: Core platform, modules, user types, companies and transaction or resource capacity.
Implementation partner, data cleanup, integrations, customizations and training.
Sandboxes, support, upgrades, AI credits and third-party services.
pitfalls: Selecting a suite before documenting the operational processes that must improve.
Treating roadmap announcements as capabilities included in today's contracted edition.
Underbudgeting migration and ongoing ownership of custom integrations.
demoQuestions: Which steps in our scenario are standard, configured, custom or unsupported?
Can you show entity consolidation and trace a total to source transactions?
Who owns integration failures, upgrades and support after implementation?
What is the complete three-year cost including AI, environments and growth?

faq.q: Can a smaller business justify ERP?
faq.a: Yes, when operational complexity creates enough manual work or control gaps. Headcount alone is a poor selection rule. Map the costly handoffs, confirm the minimum useful scope and compare the change effort with improving the existing stack.

faq.q: Is cloud deployment enough to make implementation simple?
faq.a: No. Hosting reduces some infrastructure work, but does not clean master data, decide approval rules or train staff. A successful project still needs a process owner, tested integrations and a realistic plan for operating during cutover.

faq.q: How should we compare ERP AI?
faq.a: Ask for a live demonstration of the exact task in the contracted product version. Document permissions, human approval, usage cost and supported regions. Text generation, anomaly detection and agents executing transactions solve different problems and should be described separately.

categories.name: Point of Sale
categories.description: Compare US point-of-sale systems for retail, hospitality and service businesses, including hardware, inventory and connected sales.
categories.buyerQuestion: Does the system fit your checkout, inventory and location workflow at the full operating cost?
categories.intro: Point of sale is where software, payment processing, hardware and staff behavior meet. A boutique, a restaurant and a service business all accept payments, but their day-to-day requirements differ substantially. Start by naming the sales workflow and the failure modes you must handle. A low software price can hide hardware, processing, location or add-on costs. Compare the complete setup: terminals, printers, scanners, subscriptions, payment terms and online channels. AI reporting may help an owner spot a pattern, but it cannot compensate for a checkout flow that staff struggle to use during a busy period.

criteria.label: Checkout & payment workflow
criteria.why: Fast, understandable sales and refund workflows are the operational foundation.

criteria.label: Inventory or menu management
criteria.why: Stock, modifiers and catalog handling must match the business type.

criteria.label: Staff & location controls
criteria.why: Permissions and multi-location oversight become important as teams grow.

criteria.label: Online & connected sales
criteria.why: Connected orders reduce duplicate catalogs and reconciliation work.

criteria.label: AI insights & assistance
criteria.why: Assess documented business-data assistance, not an unrelated marketing claim.

criteria.label: Operational detail
criteria.why: Specific workflow, integration and control checks beyond the established rubric.

buyingAdvice.title: Test your busiest workflow on the proposed hardware
buyingAdvice.body: Bring a cashier or shift manager to the demo. Run a purchase with a discount, split tender, return and missing barcode or modifier. For hospitality, include the exact ordering and fulfillment sequence you use rather than evaluating a retail checkout screen. Ask what works during an internet interruption and what must wait until reconnection. Request a written hardware list with installation, replacement and warranty assumptions. The system should make ordinary mistakes recoverable by the right staff member, without giving every employee unrestricted access to refunds or sensitive reports.

buyingAdvice.title: Compare the full location economics
buyingAdvice.body: Use a consistent number of locations, registers, staff accounts and online orders for every quote. Add payment processing, loyalty, messaging, delivery integrations and any required hardware financing. Confirm whether a promoted software price assumes use of the vendor's processing service or a longer commitment. Estimate the cost of adding a second location before choosing the first. If a reseller supplies the package, identify who owns the contract and support relationship. A single brand can be sold through different commercial arrangements, so a website headline is not a substitute for the actual offer.

buyingAdvice.title: Keep the catalog and reporting connected
buyingAdvice.body: Demonstrate how an item, variant, price change and return move between store and online channels. Test whether stock is reserved consistently and how a transfer between locations is recorded. Ask the finance team to reconcile a day's sales with the deposit and fee report. For AI insights, use a concrete question about stock or sales and inspect the underlying date range and records. A useful assistant must respect what the user is allowed to see. Treat vendor growth or revenue claims as examples, and measure whether the tools reduce your own reporting and ordering effort.

costDrivers: Software per location or register, staff access and specialist modules.
Hardware, installation, financing, support and replacement devices.
Processing rates, online orders, loyalty, messaging and third-party integrations.
pitfalls: Evaluating restaurant and retail systems as interchangeable because both take cards.
Ignoring hardware and processor commitments when comparing software subscriptions.
Assuming that online and store inventory synchronize without testing returns and transfers.
demoQuestions: Can a staff member complete our busiest sale and correct a mistake?
What remains usable offline, and what happens when connectivity returns?
Which contract covers hardware, payment processing and support?
Can we trace an AI insight to the actual items, dates and sales records?

faq.q: Is free POS software really free to operate?
faq.a: A no-subscription plan can still charge for payment processing, hardware and optional services. Compare the complete operating cost for your transaction volume and locations. Free can be a good starting point when its workflow fits, but it is not a complete cost statement.

faq.q: Do we need a retail-specific or restaurant-specific product?
faq.a: Choose according to workflow. Retail often emphasizes variants, purchasing and stock transfers; hospitality may emphasize menus, modifiers and kitchen flow. Ask each vendor to demonstrate your real process rather than treating these labels as a ranking.

faq.q: Should AI determine the POS decision?
faq.a: It should be one factor. Documented insights or task assistance can save work, but checkout reliability, staff permissions and accurate inventory remain central. Confirm the AI's availability and data scope in your proposed edition, then test it alongside the operational workflow.

depthMethodology.scope: Product documentation; plan inclusion must be established separately.

categories.name: Appointment Scheduling
categories.description: Compare scheduling for US sales teams, consultants, salons and service businesses, including reminders, payments and AI booking.
categories.buyerQuestion: Are you coordinating meetings, selling appointments or managing staff and service capacity?
categories.intro: Scheduling software is not one uniform category. A sales team usually needs calendar coordination and lead routing; a salon needs staff availability, service duration, deposits and a checkout workflow. A consultant may need both. Define the appointment, the people and resources involved, and the rules for changing it. Compare the plan that supports that workflow, including SMS or WhatsApp credits and payment fees where relevant. AI can answer questions or help a client book, but a conversational interface should still respect availability, cancellation rules and a clear confirmation step.

criteria.label: Self-service booking
criteria.why: Customers need a clear way to select the right service and available time.

criteria.label: Calendars, staff & resources
criteria.why: Avoid conflicts across people, locations and bookable resources.

criteria.label: Reminders & follow-up
criteria.why: Notifications, changes and follow-up help the booking remain usable.

criteria.label: Payments & deposits
criteria.why: Paid services need collection and cancellation workflows.

criteria.label: AI scheduling assistance
criteria.why: Distinguish recommendations, meeting notes and actual booking actions.

criteria.label: Operational detail
criteria.why: Specific workflow, integration and control checks beyond the established rubric.

buyingAdvice.title: Choose the scheduling model before choosing the brand
buyingAdvice.body: List whether your bookings are one-to-one meetings, team meetings, classes or paid services. Then describe staff selection, service length, buffers, rooms, equipment, recurring sessions and time zones. A tool that is excellent at finding a meeting slot may require workarounds for a treatment room or a package of classes. Test a booking from the customer's phone and a change made by staff. Include an appointment near a daylight-saving transition if your team works across US time zones. The objective is to find a model that matches normal operations without maintaining a second calendar.

buyingAdvice.title: Treat reminders and payments as a complete workflow
buyingAdvice.body: Walk through a deposit, a reschedule, a cancellation and a no-show. Decide which notifications are operational reminders and which are marketing, and confirm that the product can support your chosen permissions and preferences. Compare email, SMS and other channel allowances separately; an included reminder feature does not necessarily mean unlimited messages. Ask how refunds, saved payment details and processor fees are handled. For a service business, check the handoff from appointment to checkout and reporting. For a sales team, check the handoff into CRM and who owns the record after reassignment.

buyingAdvice.title: Measure the AI's actual role in the booking
buyingAdvice.body: An AI note-taker, an assistant that suggests meeting times and a client-facing agent that creates appointments are different products. Ask which role is available in the quoted plan. Test an unavailable time, an ambiguous service, a cancellation request and a request for a human. Require the final appointment details to be clear to the customer before commitment. If the feature consumes credits, find out whether incomplete conversations also count. Keep a normal booking path available for customers who prefer it. Evaluate the assistant by completed, correct bookings and reduced staff effort rather than the novelty of the interface.

costDrivers: Host seats, bookable staff, locations, calendars and monthly booking limits.
SMS, WhatsApp, AI conversation credits and paid marketing tools.
Payment processing, website packages, migration and specialist integrations.
pitfalls: Buying a meeting scheduler for a complex service operation without testing resources and checkout.
Assuming all reminder channels and AI conversations are unlimited.
Treating a meeting note-taker as evidence of autonomous appointment booking.
demoQuestions: Can we model our staff, buffers, rooms and cancellation rules?
How are duplicate bookings and external calendar changes handled?
What does a deposit, refund or no-show cost in our chosen plan?
Can the AI change a booking, or does it only provide information and a link?

faq.q: Can one product cover meetings and paid services?
faq.a: Sometimes, but verify the workflow. Payment integrations can make a meeting scheduler useful for consulting, while service-focused platforms may offer richer staff and resource controls. Start with the hardest booking you must support and test it end to end.

faq.q: Do customers need to buy seats?
faq.a: Usually host or staff licensing is distinct from the customer making a booking, but the pricing basis varies. Some services also cap bookings, calendars or providers. Read the plan definition and model the number of people who actually manage or host appointments.

faq.q: How should AI booking be scored?
faq.a: Score the documented task in the proposed plan. Meeting summaries deserve different treatment from an assistant that checks availability and confirms an appointment. Note credit limits, activation requirements and human handoff, and leave unverified capabilities unknown.

depthMethodology.scope: Product documentation; plan inclusion must be established separately.

categories.name: Electronic Signature
categories.description: Compare signature collection, reusable documents, approval workflows and agreement intelligence for US businesses.
categories.buyerQuestion: Do you need occasional signatures, repeatable sales documents or a controlled agreement workflow?
categories.intro: Electronic signature purchasing starts with the document workflow, not a claim that every product makes every agreement legally sufficient. A freelancer sending a few agreements needs different capabilities from a team generating proposals from CRM or managing approvals before signature. Compare sender seats, envelopes or documents, templates, authentication options, audit evidence and export. AI summaries can speed orientation, but should not replace reading important terms or professional review. Keep contract drafting, signature collection and post-signature management separate in your requirements so the quoted plan covers the tasks you actually need.

criteria.label: Send, sign & track
criteria.why: The core signing experience must work for recipients and senders.

criteria.label: Audit trail & verification options
criteria.why: Completion records, authentication and export support a controlled workflow.

criteria.label: Templates & approvals
criteria.why: Repeatable documents and routing reduce preparation effort.

criteria.label: Business-system integration
criteria.why: CRM, storage and API connections reduce duplicate data entry.

criteria.label: AI document assistance
criteria.why: Differentiate summarization, drafting and agreement-management actions.

criteria.label: Operational detail
criteria.why: Specific workflow, integration and control checks beyond the established rubric.

buyingAdvice.title: Count transactions using the vendor's unit
buyingAdvice.body: Write down how many documents, recipients and signing requests you send in an ordinary month and in a busy month. Then translate that usage into each vendor's definition of an envelope, document or transaction. A package containing several files may count differently from several separate requests. Confirm what happens when a request is voided, resent, sent in bulk or generated through an API. Compare annual allowances with monthly limits, and include the cost of adding senders. A generous headline allowance is less useful if the specific workflow uses a separately metered automation or integration.

buyingAdvice.title: Demo the full approval and evidence chain
buyingAdvice.body: Start with a document generated from a template, send it for internal approval, request a recipient correction and complete the signature. Export the signed file and the completion evidence to the repository where your team will keep them. Check who can alter templates, view agreements, resend a request or change the recipient. Ask which identity checks are available and which cost extra. Do not infer suitability for a regulated or unusual transaction from a general e-signature statement. Have your own legal or compliance owner decide the required process, then use the demo to verify the software can implement it.

buyingAdvice.title: Separate document AI from agreement execution
buyingAdvice.body: Ask the assistant to summarize a sample agreement and identify where each answer came from. Then test a changed date, an inconsistent price and a clause it cannot confidently interpret. If the product can create or send documents through an AI integration, inspect the permissions and confirmation step before a real recipient receives anything. Keep AI drafting, field detection, document search and post-signature obligation extraction as separate checklist items. Verify whether the feature belongs to the e-signature plan, a broader agreement-management product or an external AI subscription. Human approval remains essential for commitments.

costDrivers: Sender licenses, envelope or document allowances and annual commitment.
Bulk sending, API transactions, identity verification, SMS and workflow automation.
Document-generation, CRM, agreement repository and AI product tiers.
pitfalls: Equating unlimited manual signatures with unlimited API or automated transactions.
Assuming an AI summary is a complete or authoritative interpretation of an agreement.
Purchasing a basic signature plan while expecting a full contract-management platform.
demoQuestions: What counts as one billable transaction in our actual workflow?
Can we export both the completed document and its audit evidence?
Which approvals, identity checks and integrations need an upgrade or credit?
What can the AI read or send, and where does a person confirm the action?

faq.q: Is an e-signature tool the same as contract management?
faq.a: No. Signature collection is one stage. Drafting, negotiation, internal approval, searchable repositories and obligation tracking may belong to separate products or higher plans. Write down the complete lifecycle and compare the relevant modules rather than the vendor name alone.

faq.q: Are AI summaries safe to rely on for a contract decision?
faq.a: Use them to navigate the document, then verify the underlying language. A summary can omit context or misinterpret a term. The comparison evaluates documented assistance, not legal judgment, and important commitments still require appropriate human review.

faq.q: How do I compare a cheap plan with an unlimited plan?
faq.a: Calculate the cost for your real senders and workflows. Check annual versus monthly limits, bulk and API rules, templates, authentication and export. An unlimited manual workflow may still have separate charges for automation or recipient verification.

depthMethodology.scope: Product documentation; plan inclusion must be established separately.

categories.name: Benefits administration
categories.description: US enrollment, payroll deductions, plan access, and benefits reporting.
categories.buyerQuestion: Will this system improve benefits enrollment and reconciliation for our actual workforce?
categories.intro: Benefits software, an insurance broker, a benefits marketplace, and a professional employer organization solve related but different problems. Start by deciding whether you want to retain existing plans and advisors, obtain new coverage, or change the employment-service arrangement. Then compare enrollment, employee explanations, payroll deductions, and reporting. A platform fee is not the insurance premium, and a nationwide provider name does not establish that a particular plan fits every employee's location. This category covers operational software and services rather than recommending insurance coverage. Bring the benefits administrator, payroll owner, and current advisor into the evaluation early enough to catch carrier, eligibility, and renewal constraints.

criteria.label: Enrollment workflows
criteria.why: Employees need accurate enrollment and life-event workflows.

criteria.label: Payroll deduction sync
criteria.why: Deductions must follow elections and effective dates.

criteria.label: Plans & broker options
criteria.why: Existing broker and carrier relationships affect the switch.

criteria.label: Benefits visibility
criteria.why: Administrators need to reconcile enrollment and costs.

criteria.label: AI benefits assistance
criteria.why: AI explanations need plan grounding and clear limitations.

criteria.label: Operational detail
criteria.why: Specific workflow, integration and control checks beyond the established rubric.

buyingAdvice.title: Compare the operating model before the interface
buyingAdvice.body: Ask each provider to identify precisely what it supplies: software, brokerage, administration, payroll, or a PEO arrangement. Establish who handles employee questions, carrier changes, and unresolved enrollment problems. If you want to keep your broker, verify that the specific relationship and plans can be supported and whether an additional fee applies. If you want new plans, request options for your real employee locations and eligibility groups. Treat a demo's sample medical plan as an interface example, not proof of availability. Make renewal timing part of the implementation plan so the software decision does not accidentally become an unplanned coverage change.

buyingAdvice.title: Test the difficult enrollment changes
buyingAdvice.body: Demonstrate a new hire, a qualifying change, a dependent update, a waived election, and a termination using anonymized examples. Follow each change through approval, effective date, payroll deduction, and the administrator's report. Ask how retroactive corrections are surfaced and how a mismatch is reconciled. Let an employee compare plans on a phone and find the relevant documents without help from the presenter. The system should reduce confusing handoffs, but your team still needs a clear owner for exceptions. Keep a list of the carrier connections and files involved rather than accepting the word integrated without checking the actual data flow.

buyingAdvice.title: Budget for the complete benefit operation
buyingAdvice.body: Separate platform and administration charges from premiums, employer contributions, advisor fees, and optional services. A per-benefits-eligible-employee charge can behave differently from a per-enrolled-participant charge; use the correct population in the comparison. Ask how employee-count changes and renewals affect billing. For AI assistance, require answers based on your current plan documents and a visible route to a person when the information is incomplete. Do not substitute a generated explanation for the official plan information. Distinguish features available now from a vendor's coming-soon employee assistant, and include that distinction in your final purchasing decision.

costDrivers: Administration or PEO fees versus insurance premiums and employer contributions.
Existing broker integrations, participant charges, and optional services.
Carrier connections, renewal transitions, and payroll reconciliation work.
pitfalls: Treating benefits access as guaranteed coverage for every location.
Comparing PEO fees directly with software-only administration.
Accepting generic AI explanations without the relevant current plan documents.
demoQuestions: Can we retain our exact broker and plans, and at what cost?
Show a life-event change reaching the correct payroll deduction.
Who resolves a mismatch between enrollment and carrier records?
Which AI answers cite our documents, and how does an employee reach a person?

faq.q: Are premiums included in software pricing?
faq.a: Usually the platform price and insurance costs are different items. Obtain a quote that separates each fee and contribution.

faq.q: Is a PEO the same as benefits software?
faq.a: No. It is a different service arrangement. Evaluate its responsibilities and contract separately from interface features.

faq.q: Can we keep our existing benefits?
faq.a: Some providers support transfers or broker connections, subject to eligibility and plan support. Verify your specific arrangement before committing.

categories.name: Time & attendance
categories.description: Time capture, scheduling, approvals, and payroll handoff for US teams.
categories.buyerQuestion: Can managers produce accurate approved time without adding friction for employees?
categories.intro: Time tracking for client projects and time attendance for shift workers share a clock but serve different decisions. A consultancy may prioritize billable hours and project budgets, while a restaurant or retailer needs coverage, shift swaps, breaks, and payroll-ready approvals. Start with the places people work, the devices they can use, and the manager who fixes a missing entry. Then define how scheduling, approved time, pay rules, and payroll fit together. A schedule is planned work; a time record is reported work; an approved timesheet is a controlled handoff. Comparing those separately avoids buying an attractive calendar that leaves the difficult administrative work unchanged.

criteria.label: Time capture
criteria.why: Capture should fit the work location and devices.

criteria.label: Shift or resource scheduling
criteria.why: Coverage and availability need a usable planning process.

criteria.label: Timesheet approvals
criteria.why: Managers need a controlled correction and review step.

criteria.label: Payroll handoff
criteria.why: Approved time must reach payroll or an export.

criteria.label: AI scheduling & assistance
criteria.why: AI needs operational inputs and manager review.

criteria.label: Operational detail
criteria.why: Specific workflow, integration and control checks beyond the established rubric.

buyingAdvice.title: Match the clock to the workplace
buyingAdvice.body: Test the exact devices employees will use: a shared kiosk, phone, browser, or point-of-sale terminal. Include a missed punch, poor connectivity, a location change, and a manager correction in the demonstration. Ask what location or biometric information the selected method collects and how your team configures access and retention. Those choices deserve an operational and privacy review for your workforce; a product feature alone does not establish suitability. If workers track client projects, check whether time can be assigned accurately to the project and task without making the daily entry process too cumbersome.

buyingAdvice.title: Follow one schedule through to payroll
buyingAdvice.body: Build a normal week using employee availability, required roles, time off, and an unexpected absence. Have a worker request a swap and a manager approve it. Then replace the planned hours with actual clocked time, correct an entry, and export the approved period. Check employee identifiers, earning codes, multiple rates, and the destination payroll period. An integration logo does not show which fields transfer or who reconciles failures. Ask for the support owner on both sides. For US operations across locations, have your payroll or workforce specialist review how your real policies are configured before trusting automatic calculations.

buyingAdvice.title: Distinguish automation from AI and price both
buyingAdvice.body: Automatic reminders, recurring schedules, and rule-based approvals can be useful without being generative AI. Ask a vendor to show what its AI actually does: forecast demand, suggest staffing, answer questions, or draft a schedule. Then provide incomplete availability and conflicting requests to see how it handles uncertainty. Managers should be able to inspect and change recommendations before publication. Normalize per-location pricing against per-user pricing at your actual size, including inactive or seasonal staff where billed. Include payroll, advanced scheduling, reporting, and AI add-ons, and identify introductory AI access that could become a separate paid feature later.

costDrivers: Per-user versus per-location billing and seasonal headcount.
Payroll, advanced scheduling, kiosks, reporting, and administration tiers.
Manager time spent resolving missing records and integration exceptions.
pitfalls: Treating planned shifts as approved payable hours.
Assuming every payroll connector transfers every earning code.
Calling rule-based scheduling AI without a documented AI capability.
demoQuestions: Show missed-punch correction and its approval history.
Can employees swap shifts without exposing everyone else's private information?
Which exact fields transfer to our payroll product?
What happens when AI receives incomplete availability or conflicting constraints?

faq.q: Can a free timer replace attendance software?
faq.a: It may cover simple hour capture. Scheduling, approvals, payroll export, and role controls often require additional capabilities or paid tiers.

faq.q: Is automatic scheduling always AI?
faq.a: No. We credit AI only where the vendor documents an AI capability and describe its scope separately from routine automation.

faq.q: What should a pilot measure?
faq.a: Measure missed entries, correction effort, manager approval time, and successful payroll handoffs using a representative team.

categories.name: Business intelligence
categories.description: Data connections, semantic models, dashboards, governance, and analytical AI.
categories.buyerQuestion: Can business users get dependable answers without creating another set of conflicting metrics?
categories.intro: Business intelligence should connect a decision to a defined metric, a trusted dataset, and a responsible owner. Start with the questions you need to answer, the systems that hold the data, and the people who will publish versus consume reports. A dashboard can look polished while joining incompatible dates, customer definitions, or revenue measures. Compare data connectivity, modeling, visualization, access controls, and AI separately. These platforms also use different commercial models: named users, capacity, data volume, or consumption credits. A small authoring price does not establish the total cost of sharing reports across the company or embedding them in a customer-facing product.

criteria.label: Data connectivity
criteria.why: Sources and refresh behavior determine usable coverage.

criteria.label: Modeling & preparation
criteria.why: Shared definitions prevent conflicting answers.

criteria.label: Reports & exploration
criteria.why: Users need useful exploration rather than static pictures.

criteria.label: Governed access
criteria.why: Sensitive rows and publishing rights need control.

criteria.label: AI analytics
criteria.why: AI answers require grounded models and explicit licensing.

criteria.label: Operational detail
criteria.why: Specific workflow, integration and control checks beyond the established rubric.

buyingAdvice.title: Start with one disputed business metric
buyingAdvice.body: Pick a metric that currently produces different answers in different meetings, such as active customers or recognized sales. Write its definition, time basis, exclusions, and owner. Ask each finalist to connect the required sources, implement the definition, and explain a discrepancy at the record level. Include a realistic data refresh and a schema change. This exposes the modeling and operating work behind the dashboard. If you already use a warehouse or lakehouse, establish which transformations should stay there and which belong in the BI model. Keep the architecture understandable enough that another analyst can maintain it.

buyingAdvice.title: Price the audience and the workload together
buyingAdvice.body: Count creators, editors, internal viewers, external viewers, and embedded customers. Ask which licenses each role needs and whether capacity changes that requirement. Then estimate data volume, refresh frequency, model size, query concurrency, and AI usage. Use the same representative workload in each trial; comparing a per-user plan with a consumption platform by sticker price alone is misleading. Include warehouse compute, connectors, gateway operation, and administration where applicable. Ask how the platform surfaces limits and how you would investigate a sudden cost increase. A forecast should include normal use and a busy reporting period.

buyingAdvice.title: Validate AI against governed questions
buyingAdvice.body: Give the AI a set of known questions with verified answers, including ambiguous terms and a request for data the user should not access. Inspect the generated query or explanation and the source model where available. Check whether the capability answers questions, generates calculations, builds charts, or takes actions in another system; these are distinct functions. Verify the necessary capacity, edition, region, permissions, and credit allowance. Some experiences are previews or promotions rather than stable entitlements. Keep a human owner for metric definitions, and measure how frequently AI requires clarification or correction before making it the default route for important business decisions.

costDrivers: Creator, explorer, viewer, embedded, and capacity licensing.
Data storage, refreshes, queries, warehouse compute, and connectors.
AI capacity or token allowances plus modeling and governance work.
pitfalls: Treating a visually convincing dashboard as proof of correct definitions.
Assuming a per-user license automatically includes analytical Copilot.
Comparing consumption credits across vendors as if they were equivalent units.
demoQuestions: Reconcile this metric to the underlying records and explain the difference.
What does our complete internal and external audience cost?
Show row-level access and how it applies to AI questions.
Which workloads and AI requests consume additional capacity or credits?

faq.q: Is Looker the same product as Looker Studio?
faq.a: No. Evaluate the specific product and commercial model in the quote; this catalog's Looker profile covers the enterprise BI platform.

faq.q: Does an AI assistant remove the need for modeling?
faq.a: No. Clear definitions and permissions remain essential inputs. Poorly prepared data can produce confident but incorrect answers.

faq.q: Should we choose the cheapest authoring seat?
faq.a: Calculate the full audience and workload cost. Sharing, embedded access, refresh requirements, and AI can change the economics substantially.

categories.name: Business phone systems
categories.description: Compare US business calling, shared numbers, routing, integrations and AI assistance without confusing a seat subscription with the entire phone bill.
categories.buyerQuestion: Which phone system fits US calling, routing, teamwork, and administration?
categories.intro: A business phone system should make incoming calls reach the right person and let staff work consistently across devices. Buying decisions often begin with a seat price, but everyday suitability depends on routing, shared numbers, administration and the team's existing applications. A small service business may value a shared calling-and-texting inbox. A distributed company may need multi-level menus, queues, location controls and centralized provisioning. AI summaries and receptionists can reduce particular tasks, but they do not establish call quality or reliability. Treat those as separate questions for a pilot. This category assesses documented functions and plan boundaries, with US calling eligibility and add-on costs considered explicitly.

criteria.label: US business calling
criteria.why: US numbers and calling plans must match the organization's actual destinations and volume.

criteria.label: Team calling and messaging
criteria.why: Shared lines, messaging and device continuity determine how a team works together.

criteria.label: Call routing and administration
criteria.why: Routing and administrative controls turn individual numbers into an operable business service.

criteria.label: Business application connections
criteria.why: Connected applications reduce duplicate work when they support the exact required data exchange.

criteria.label: AI call assistance and agents
criteria.why: AI should have a defined job, with plan limits and human oversight appropriate to that job.

criteria.label: Operational detail
criteria.why: Specific workflow, integration and control checks beyond the established rubric.

buyingAdvice.title: Map your current call flows before requesting quotes
buyingAdvice.body: Draw what should happen to a sales inquiry, an existing-customer issue and an after-hours call. Include holidays, unavailable employees and calls that wait too long. Identify which numbers must stay with the business and who owns the records needed to move them. Ask each vendor to configure the same sample flow. Check the experience on the devices employees actually use, including headsets and mobile apps. A feature list can show that routing exists without showing whether your team can maintain it. Assign an administrator and a backup, then have both make a routine change during the evaluation.

buyingAdvice.title: Separate calling, messaging and AI requirements
buyingAdvice.body: Document calling destinations, business texting needs, shared inbox requirements and meeting tools independently. Unlimited calling language may apply to a specified geography and remain subject to the provider's terms; it should not be read as unlimited use of every channel or feature. Team SMS, advanced queues, CRM connections and AI receptionists may have separate packaging. For AI, distinguish post-call summaries from an agent that talks to customers and takes actions. Demonstrate the exact function you intend to buy. A recording or summary should also be discoverable, access-controlled and manageable under your organization's retention process rather than accumulating without an owner.

buyingAdvice.title: Pilot the migration and the operating routine
buyingAdvice.body: Use a limited group and temporary numbers to verify device behavior, routing, transfers and support responsiveness before moving critical numbers. Ask how porting dates, rollback options and service interruptions are handled. Have the team rehearse an internet outage and an employee departure. Confirm how to revoke access, reassign numbers and retrieve needed business records. Review the full invoice structure: licenses, numbers, usage, hardware, AI and applicable fees. A low introductory quote can hide a different renewal cost or commitment. Keep a written inventory of included features and require the proposal to identify paid add-ons needed for your demonstrated workflow.

costDrivers: Per-user subscriptions, billing commitment, renewal terms and additional numbers.
International or metered calling, texting, hardware and applicable fees.
AI receptionists, advanced queues, integrations and migration assistance.
pitfalls: Assuming every feature on a product page is included in the entry plan.
Moving critical numbers before verifying the target call flows and support process.
Treating an AI summary feature as an autonomous receptionist or full contact center.
demoQuestions: Configure our after-hours and unanswered-call flow, including an unavailable transfer target.
Which required features cost extra beyond the quoted seats?
Show how a departing employee's number, messages and recordings are reassigned.
What is the number-porting plan and how will we handle an unexpected delay?

faq.q: Is a cloud PBX the same as a contact center?
faq.a: They overlap, but a contact center typically serves more specialized agent and customer-service workflows. Do not infer advanced workforce, quality or queue functionality from the phone-system label. Compare the operational features required by your team and the exact products included in the quote.

faq.q: Should a small business choose the cheapest seat?
faq.a: Only after checking the complete workflow and bill. A plan that needs extra users, integration tiers or an AI add-on can cost more than its headline suggests. Conversely, an expensive bundle offers little value when the team will not use its additional capabilities.

faq.q: How much should AI affect the choice?
faq.a: Our capability model gives AI 15% of category weight. That reflects a useful dimension without allowing AI to override core calling and routing needs. It is not a measured productivity score. Test summaries or receptionist behavior using your own calls and review process.

categories.name: Recruiting & applicant tracking
categories.description: Candidate sourcing, hiring pipelines, interview coordination, and recruiting analytics.
categories.buyerQuestion: Which recruiting system improves coordination while preserving a clear, reviewable hiring process?
categories.intro: A recruiting system should help people make and document hiring decisions, not simply collect more applications. Start with the roles you hire, the number of open requisitions, your sourcing channels, and the people involved in interviews and offers. A small business hiring a few employees needs different administration from a recruiting organization managing multiple teams and talent pools. Compare sourcing, pipeline management, interview coordination, analytics, and AI separately. Also separate the applicant tracking system from paid job advertising, assessments, background checks, texting, and interview recording. These may be connected to the same interface while carrying different fees, permissions, and operational responsibilities.

criteria.label: Sourcing & talent pools
criteria.why: Teams need to find and re-engage relevant candidates.

criteria.label: Applicant pipeline
criteria.why: A consistent pipeline supports traceable decisions.

criteria.label: Interview coordination
criteria.why: Scheduling and feedback create frequent bottlenecks.

criteria.label: Recruiting analytics
criteria.why: Stage and source metrics help improve the process.

criteria.label: AI recruiting assistance
criteria.why: AI assistance needs review, clear scope, and usage limits.

criteria.label: Operational detail
criteria.why: Specific workflow, integration and control checks beyond the established rubric.

buyingAdvice.title: Map a role from approval to accepted offer
buyingAdvice.body: Choose a realistic requisition with several interviewers, a hiring-manager change, and an external candidate. Show how the opening is approved, published, sourced, scheduled, evaluated, and closed. Inspect the candidate experience as well as the recruiter's screen. Confirm who can see interview feedback before submitting their own and how scorecards relate to the role's criteria. If your process includes agency candidates or referrals, test those paths. The goal is a repeatable workflow that preserves context, not merely a fast way to advance a candidate through stages. Include the HR handoff after an offer is accepted.

buyingAdvice.title: Measure the funnel rather than admiring the dashboard
buyingAdvice.body: Define how your team measures time in stage, source quality, interviewer workload, and offer acceptance. Ask the vendor to reproduce those definitions on sample data, including reopened jobs, merged candidate records, and candidates considered for more than one role. Check whether reports can be filtered by the permissions of the person viewing them. For migration, decide which historical applications, attachments, notes, and consent records you need and how duplicates will be handled. A system with extensive analytics still needs consistent stages and disciplined data entry to produce useful comparisons across teams and hiring periods.

buyingAdvice.title: Evaluate AI as a controlled recruiting capability
buyingAdvice.body: Ask what the AI reads, what it recommends, and what it changes. Drafting outreach, summarizing interviews, suggesting scheduling slots, screening applications, and conducting voice interviews have different implications. Use a varied sample and have recruiters review the output against the documented job criteria. Keep evidence for why a person advances or is rejected and establish a route for questions or correction. Review the relevant employment and privacy requirements with your specialists before enabling candidate-facing or decision-support automation. Check whether AI is included, metered by candidate or action, or sold separately; a trial allowance should not be treated as the production budget.

costDrivers: Company-size or recruiter-seat pricing and contract commitment.
Job advertising, texting, assessments, recording, and background services.
AI screening credits, migration, integrations, and recruiting operations.
pitfalls: Treating an AI ranking as an objective measure of candidate quality.
Comparing platform fees without paid sourcing and interview add-ons.
Migrating inconsistent pipeline stages and expecting comparable historical reports.
demoQuestions: Show the complete path from approved requisition to HR onboarding.
How are duplicate candidates and multiple applications represented?
Can we inspect and override an AI recommendation with a recorded reason?
Which actions consume credits, and what happens when the allowance is exhausted?

faq.q: Does every business need a standalone ATS?
faq.a: Not always. A capable HR suite may cover a modest hiring workflow; dedicated sourcing, scheduling, or analytics can justify a specialist platform.

faq.q: Is AI screening the same as an AI notetaker?
faq.a: No. Screening evaluates applications against criteria; notetaking captures and summarizes interviews. Compare their scope, controls, and costs separately.

faq.q: Can recruiting software guarantee fair hiring?
faq.a: No software comparison can guarantee that outcome. Your criteria, implementation, review practices, and applicable requirements remain important.

categories.name: Workflow automation
categories.description: Connect apps, orchestrate processes, operate automations, and govern AI actions.
categories.buyerQuestion: Which automation platform can run our real workflows reliably at an understandable cost?
categories.intro: Automation platforms connect applications and coordinate work, but their operating models differ. A simple lead handoff can suit a business-owned no-code workflow; a process spanning finance, employee access, and private infrastructure may need stronger engineering and governance. Start with a written process, its source of truth, expected volume, and the person who owns failures. Then compare connectors, logic, operations, access controls, and AI. An integration count is only a starting point: the necessary trigger, action, fields, and authentication must be supported. A successful demo run also says little about duplicate events, expired credentials, rate limits, or recovery after an upstream system changes.

criteria.label: Connectors & APIs
criteria.why: Actual supported operations matter more than logo counts.

criteria.label: Workflow logic
criteria.why: Branches and transformations determine process coverage.

criteria.label: Monitoring & recovery
criteria.why: Failures need visible, recoverable handling.

criteria.label: Governance & access
criteria.why: Shared credentials and changes require ownership.

criteria.label: AI workflow capabilities
criteria.why: AI agents need tool boundaries, controls, and cost visibility.

criteria.label: Operational detail
criteria.why: Specific workflow, integration and control checks beyond the established rubric.

buyingAdvice.title: Document the workflow and its failure paths
buyingAdvice.body: Write the trigger, required inputs, decision rules, actions, and expected outcome before selecting a platform. Add the cases people currently fix manually: missing fields, duplicate submissions, rejected approvals, and unavailable systems. Ask each finalist to run those cases and show the execution history. Inspect what can be replayed and how duplicate side effects are prevented. Assign a business owner who can decide what the workflow should do and an operator who can diagnose failures. Start with a bounded process that can be reversed or reviewed, then expand once your team understands its behavior and costs.

buyingAdvice.title: Normalize billing using the same sample workload
buyingAdvice.body: Count completed business outcomes and the steps required for each, including loops, retries, polling, AI calls, and file processing. Then apply each vendor's current billing rules: a task, credit, execution, and bot are different units. Include external model charges if you bring your own AI provider, plus hosting and administration for self-managed deployments. Model a normal month and a burst month, and ask whether reaching a limit pauses work or creates overage charges. Record which administrative features require a higher tier. A low subscription price can still be expensive if the workflow processes many records or requires constant maintenance.

buyingAdvice.title: Give agents narrow tools and visible approval points
buyingAdvice.body: AI can help build a workflow, classify information inside a fixed process, or select actions dynamically as an agent. Evaluate these separately. Give the agent only the data and tools needed for its task, and require review before consequential external actions. Test ambiguous instructions and untrusted content entering the workflow. Check logs for what the model saw, which tool it called, and why the run stopped. Ask how credentials are shared, how development differs from production, and how a departed employee's access is removed without breaking every workflow. An agent is an operating system component that needs ownership, not a substitute for one.

costDrivers: Tasks, credits, executions, bots, concurrency, and overages.
External model tokens, hosting, connectors, and premium capabilities.
Monitoring, maintenance, credential management, and implementation effort.
pitfalls: Comparing unlike billing units without a representative workflow.
Counting an app logo as proof that the needed action is supported.
Letting a single employee's personal credentials own critical automations.
demoQuestions: Run duplicate, malformed, and failed inputs and show recovery.
What does this exact workflow cost at normal and peak volume?
How do we separate development, review, and production access?
Which AI actions need approval and what is recorded in the execution log?

faq.q: Is a workflow execution the same as a task?
faq.a: No. Vendors measure different units. Reprice the same sample process under each platform's rules instead of comparing raw allowance numbers.

faq.q: Is self-hosting automatically cheaper?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Include infrastructure, patching, backups, monitoring, and engineering time alongside any software license.

faq.q: Should every step use AI?
faq.a: No. Use deterministic rules where the outcome is known, and reserve AI for work that benefits from interpretation or generation with appropriate review.

depthMethodology.scope: Product documentation; plan inclusion must be established separately.

categories.name: Spend & Expense Management
categories.description: Compare corporate spending controls, receipts, reimbursements, bills and accounting handoffs for US finance teams.
categories.buyerQuestion: Do you need to control spend before purchase, process expenses afterward or connect the entire payables workflow?
categories.intro: Spend management covers several related jobs: authorizing purchases, issuing cards, collecting receipts, reimbursing employees and paying vendors. Products overlap, but a strong expense-reporting tool is not automatically a complete procurement or accounts-payable system. Decide which workflow is breaking down and whether employees will use a vendor-issued card or existing cards. US eligibility and underwriting can affect access to financial products; a software plan does not guarantee approval. Compare the operational controls and integration depth, then evaluate AI on the specific receipt, policy-review or coding task it performs.

criteria.label: Budgets, policies & approvals
criteria.why: Control who can spend and how exceptions are approved.

criteria.label: Receipts & reimbursements
criteria.why: Reduce missing documentation and employee reimbursement effort.

criteria.label: Vendor bills & payments
criteria.why: Distinguish employee expense tools from a complete payables workflow.

criteria.label: Accounting synchronization
criteria.why: Reliable mappings and error handling matter at close.

criteria.label: AI capture, review & coding
criteria.why: Assess the task, review boundary and product tier rather than the AI label.

criteria.label: Operational detail
criteria.why: Specific workflow, integration and control checks beyond the established rubric.

buyingAdvice.title: Choose where in the spending process to intervene
buyingAdvice.body: Map a purchase from request to approval, card charge, receipt, accounting entry and payment. Identify whether the problem is unauthorized spend, missing documentation or a slow close. A card-led platform can place limits before a purchase, while a reimbursement workflow works after an employee has paid. Many businesses need both. Test a department budget, an exception approval, a personal-card expense and an employee leaving the company. Confirm whether the financial product is available to your business and whether adopting it is required to obtain the advertised software price or functionality.

buyingAdvice.title: Make the accounting integration earn its place
buyingAdvice.body: Use a real chart of accounts and a sanitized set of departments, projects and entities during the demo. Submit a receipt with several expense types and examine how it appears in the ledger. Then edit it after synchronization and observe the correction workflow. Ask who resolves a failed sync, how duplicates are prevented and whether attachments travel with the record. A named integration is only the beginning; the direction, supported fields, timing and error handling determine whether it removes work. Compare these details before counting the integration as a complete replacement for manual reconciliation.

buyingAdvice.title: Put AI review into a controlled exception process
buyingAdvice.body: Test a duplicate receipt, a missing business purpose, an out-of-policy item and a legitimate exception. Ask the AI to explain the source of its suggestion and show what remains for a person to approve. Receipt extraction, automatic coding and autonomous policy enforcement have different consequences. Start with a narrow pilot and measure correction rates, review time and missing-document follow-up. Confirm which advanced features require a paid tier and which users are billed. Keep a way for employees to dispute a classification so automation does not turn an ambiguous receipt into an unexplained rejection.

costDrivers: Licensed or active users, platform fees and product tiers.
Card eligibility, payment methods, reimbursements, international transfers and optional travel.
ERP connectors, entity structure, procurement modules and implementation.
pitfalls: Assuming free software means every payment method and financial product is free or available.
Treating an expense app as a full accounts-payable or procurement system.
Counting an integration without checking fields, attachments and correction behavior.
demoQuestions: Can we approve a request before spending and handle a legitimate exception?
Can employees use existing cards, and what changes if they do?
How does a corrected expense synchronize to our ledger and entity structure?
Which AI decisions are suggestions, which are automatic, and how can we reverse them?

faq.q: Do we have to replace corporate cards?
faq.a: It depends on the product and desired workflow. Some platforms center on their own cards; others support connected cards or reimbursement. Compare the exact path you intend to use, including eligibility, controls and the price attached to it.

faq.q: Is an accounts-payable product also an expense platform?
faq.a: Sometimes a vendor offers both, but they can be separately priced products. Vendor bills, employee reimbursements and purchase approvals have different users and controls. Confirm each workflow and the integration between them in the proposed package.

faq.q: Can AI approve all employee spending?
faq.a: That should be a deliberate policy decision, not a default assumption. Verify the product's approval boundaries and exception handling. Start with well-defined cases, inspect errors and preserve a human review path for ambiguous or unusual transactions.

categories.name: Ecommerce Platforms
categories.description: Compare storefronts, checkout, catalog operations and extensibility for US merchants, from a first store to complex commerce.
categories.buyerQuestion: Which platform fits your catalog, channels and operating team at the cost of your next growth stage?
categories.intro: An ecommerce platform must do more than produce an attractive homepage. Your decision connects catalog structure, checkout, payments, inventory, fulfillment, returns, marketing and finance. A hosted platform reduces some operational work; an open-source stack gives more control but requires someone to own hosting, updates and extensions. Compare the workflow and total cost at your expected sales volume, not only today's subscription. Pricing can include sales thresholds, additional provider fees or paid extensions. AI creation tools can speed setup and content, but the quality of the catalog and the reliability of order operations still determine the customer experience.

criteria.label: Storefront & catalog
criteria.why: Product structure and editing must fit how you merchandise.

criteria.label: Checkout & payments
criteria.why: A reliable purchase flow and suitable payment options are central.

criteria.label: Orders, inventory & fulfillment
criteria.why: Manage the sale after checkout, including stock and returns.

criteria.label: Apps, APIs & customization
criteria.why: Extensions and custom interfaces affect flexibility and maintenance.

criteria.label: AI creation & commerce assistance
criteria.why: Separate copy generation, business analysis and approved operational actions.

criteria.label: Operational detail
criteria.why: Specific workflow, integration and control checks beyond the established rubric.

buyingAdvice.title: Start with catalog and fulfillment complexity
buyingAdvice.body: Create a representative product set with variants, bundles or subscriptions if you sell them. Add a promotion, a partial shipment, a return and an item that is available in a store but not in the warehouse. Ask each vendor to demonstrate the exact flow and identify paid extensions. If you sell wholesale, include account-specific terms and catalog requirements rather than assuming a B2B label covers them. Test the storefront on a phone and check how staff update content without development help. The right platform should fit the people who will run the catalog every week.

buyingAdvice.title: Build a growth-sensitive cost model
buyingAdvice.body: Use the same order count, gross merchandise value, average ticket and payment mix for each option. Include subscription, processing, platform fees, themes, apps, shipping tools and maintenance. Verify whether sales volume can trigger an automatic plan change and whether particular payment providers incur additional charges. For an open-source option, budget hosting, backups, security updates and extension compatibility work. Separate a one-time implementation cost from recurring operations. A plan that is inexpensive at launch may change substantially at the next sales threshold, so include a second scenario that represents a successful year.

buyingAdvice.title: Give AI a bounded merchandising job
buyingAdvice.body: Try product descriptions, image preparation, navigation changes or a question about sales performance. Check the factual accuracy of generated claims, variants, dimensions and return terms before publication. If an assistant can change store settings or create campaigns, inspect how it asks for approval and how changes can be reversed. Distinguish native features from external plugins and their separate costs. AI is useful when it reduces a repeatable task while preserving control over the storefront. It is not evidence that the platform has the inventory, checkout or integration behavior your business requires.

costDrivers: Subscription and sales-volume thresholds, payment processing and platform-provider fees.
Paid apps, themes, fulfillment tools, B2B capabilities and marketing usage.
Implementation, hosting or maintenance, migrations and integration ownership.
pitfalls: Choosing by visual templates before testing orders, returns and catalog structure.
Repeating old pricing claims after plan names or payment-provider fees change.
Treating open-source licensing as zero operating cost or AI-generated copy as verified product data.
demoQuestions: Can we run our complex product, order and return examples without hidden extensions?
What changes in the bill when sales volume doubles or we add another channel?
Which payment-provider fees and checkout restrictions apply to our plan?
Can we inspect and undo AI-generated content or operational changes?

faq.q: Is a hosted platform better than open source?
faq.a: Neither model wins universally. Hosted platforms package infrastructure and standard operations; open source can give greater control but needs maintenance ownership. Compare the required workflow, extension risk and internal skills, then budget the complete operating model.

faq.q: What does a no-transaction-fee claim mean?
faq.a: Read the current conditions carefully. Payment processing remains a separate cost, and platform fees may depend on provider, plan or order type. Use the live official schedule and your actual provider mix rather than an old comparison headline.

faq.q: Can AI build a store that is ready to sell?
faq.a: It can accelerate layout and content, but a merchant still needs to verify product facts, payment setup, shipping, returns and order handling. Test a complete purchase and refund before launch. AI assistance is one capability within a broader operating system.

buyingAdvice.body: Separate AI-answer monitoring from AI-generated writing.

costDrivers: Projects and tracked keywords
Crawl, API and export allowances
Extra users, AI prompt checks and reporting add-ons
pitfalls: Comparing weekly ranks with daily ranks
Treating estimated traffic as audited traffic
Assuming an AI content tool also measures AI answer visibility

faq.q: What does the score measure?
faq.a: Documented capabilities against this category's weighted checks. It is not a customer rating or a hands-on performance benchmark.

faq.q: Are all features included in the starting price?
faq.a: No. Read the evidence beside each check and the plan comparison. A product-level score can include capabilities available only in higher plans or paid add-ons.

faq.q: How should I use unknown results?
faq.a: Ask the supplier to demonstrate the workflow. Unknown means the reviewed documentation does not establish the capability; it does not prove absence.

costDrivers: Renewal rate and prepaid term
Storage, websites and compute limits
Backup, email, priority support and AI token allowances
pitfalls: Comparing a four-year promotion with monthly renewal
Assuming unlimited traffic means unlimited compute
Overwriting new live orders during a full staging deployment

faq.q: What does the score measure?
faq.a: Documented capabilities against this category's weighted checks. It is not a customer rating or a hands-on performance benchmark.

faq.q: Are all features included in the starting price?
faq.a: No. Read the evidence beside each check and the plan comparison. A product-level score can include capabilities available only in higher plans or paid add-ons.

faq.q: How should I use unknown results?
faq.a: Ask the supplier to demonstrate the workflow. Unknown means the reviewed documentation does not establish the capability; it does not prove absence.

depthMethodology.scope: Product documentation; plan inclusion must be established separately.

categories.name: Cold email and sales outreach
categories.summary: Compare tools for personalised prospecting from connected sales mailboxes, follow-up sequences and reply handling.
categories.buyerQuestion: Which platform can run relevant prospecting sequences with controlled delivery, clear reply ownership and reviewable AI?
categories.context: This category assesses outbound sales operations. Permission-based newsletters and customer lifecycle campaigns belong in email marketing; a lead database alone is not a complete outreach platform. Product capability does not prove that a particular contact source or campaign is lawful.

buyingAdvice.title: Selection question 1
buyingAdvice.body: Test a reply during a waiting step and confirm subsequent messages stop.

buyingAdvice.title: Selection question 2
buyingAdvice.body: Budget for mailbox subscriptions, domains, enrichment and client workspaces as well as the sending plan.

buyingAdvice.title: Selection question 3
buyingAdvice.body: Use reply quality and qualified conversations in a controlled pilot; open rates alone can be distorted.

costDrivers: Monthly new recipients or total email volume.
Connected LinkedIn accounts, AI/enrichment credits and paid integrations.
Mailbox infrastructure, warm-up capacity and agency workspaces.
pitfalls: Unlimited connected inboxes does not remove provider sending limits.
Verification and warm-up do not guarantee inbox placement or consent.
A unified inbox may lack assignment, internal notes or client permissions.

faq.q: Is cold-email software the same as newsletter software?
faq.a: No. These tools primarily coordinate sales-mailbox sequences and replies. Newsletter products focus on subscriptions, campaign design and customer journeys.

faq.q: Does email verification prove permission to contact someone?
faq.a: No. It checks address quality; the sender must separately establish the appropriate basis and respect opt-outs.

faq.q: How is AI assessed?
faq.a: Drafting, reply categorisation, prospect context and pre-send review are separate checks. A generic AI-writing claim does not satisfy every check.

categories.description: Compare tools for personalised prospecting from connected sales mailboxes, follow-up sequences and reply handling.
categories.intro: This category assesses outbound sales operations. Permission-based newsletters and customer lifecycle campaigns belong in email marketing; a lead database alone is not a complete outreach platform. Product capability does not prove that a particular contact source or campaign is lawful.
demoQuestions: Prevent a prospect from receiving overlapping sequences or honour a shared suppression record. Demonstrate this with a test prospect.
Inspect an individual recipient's rendered email and detect missing variables before release. Demonstrate this with a test prospect.
Route follow-ups using engagement, a meeting outcome or prospect data. Demonstrate this with a test prospect.
Split prospects between variants and report variant outcomes. Demonstrate this with a test prospect.
Configure and inspect mailbox warm-up separately from prospect sends. Demonstrate this with a test prospect.
Pause, restrict or alert on deteriorating mailbox or bounce health. Demonstrate this with a test prospect.
Export identifiable lead outcomes and exchange campaign data through a documented API or events. Demonstrate this with a test prospect.
Restrict a team member or client to the intended campaign or workspace data. Demonstrate this with a test prospect.
Generate content using identified prospect fields or researched source context. Demonstrate this with a test prospect.
Review AI-generated messages or campaign changes before they are launched. Demonstrate this with a test prospect.

depthMethodology.scope: Product documentation; plan inclusion must be established separately.

categories.name: Team chat and collaboration
categories.summary: Compare persistent team conversations, searchable knowledge, meetings and administrative control.
categories.buyerQuestion: Can the team find, discuss and act on work without losing conversation context or access boundaries?
categories.context: Team chat covers channels and direct messages. Project platforms qualify when conversations are native, but linked meeting tools and project-only search should remain explicit.

buyingAdvice.title: Selection question 1
buyingAdvice.body: Test a private discussion with an external guest.

buyingAdvice.title: Selection question 2
buyingAdvice.body: Search an old decision and export the evidence.

buyingAdvice.title: Selection question 3
buyingAdvice.body: Check retention, SSO and meeting limits on the quoted plan.

costDrivers: Paid members and guest licensing
Meeting capacity, recordings and storage
SSO, retention and audit tiers
pitfalls: Unlimited history does not imply a complete export.
An external meeting integration is not a native calling service.
A bot or automation rule is not evidence of AI reasoning.

faq.q: Is a project chat comparable to a dedicated messenger?
faq.a: For task-centred discussion, sometimes. Check cross-project communication, meeting tools and retention separately.

faq.q: Does unlimited history include exports?
faq.a: No. Export scopes can exclude private channels or direct messages.

faq.q: How is AI assessed?
faq.a: Credit requires a documented conversation workflow, access boundaries and a way to review resulting actions.

depthMethodology.scope: Product documentation; plan inclusion must be established separately.

categories.name: Business password management
categories.summary: Compare workforce vaults, controlled sharing, identity integration and auditable access.
categories.buyerQuestion: Can employees use business credentials while administrators control onboarding, sharing and departure?
categories.context: Workforce password vaults differ from developer secret managers. The AI section checks agent runtime access, restricted scope and attribution; ordinary autofill is not sufficient.

buyingAdvice.title: Selection question 1
buyingAdvice.body: Test access removal and ownership transfer with a departing user.

buyingAdvice.title: Selection question 2
buyingAdvice.body: Verify what a shared-folder viewer can reveal or copy.

buyingAdvice.title: Selection question 3
buyingAdvice.body: Export a real administrative event before selecting the audit tier.

costDrivers: Minimum seats and subscription term
SSO, provisioning and audit tier
Data-region and deployment requirements
pitfalls: Nested folders may inherit broader permissions.
Recovery does not guarantee selective ownership transfer.
A business vault is not automatically an AI-agent secret broker.

faq.q: Are passkeys and passwords the same comparison?
faq.a: Both can be managed in a workforce vault, but supported platforms and transfer paths differ.

faq.q: What should an offboarding test include?
faq.a: Remove sign-in access, inspect shared-item permissions and transfer the business records that must remain.

faq.q: Why assess AI here?
faq.a: Agents need narrowly scoped credentials and attributable access. Those controls must be documented separately.

decisionAid.heading: Accessibility AI: credits, permissions and page data

rows.question: Will Deque AI stop when credits run out?
rows.decision: Pro/Web subscriptions use seat-related monthly credits for selected advanced operations; unused credits expire. New charged work waits after exhaustion while in-flight work finishes and ordinary axe-core checks remain available.
rows.boundary: Numeric allocation and additional-credit prices were not established. Classification of roles, table headers and form pairs is documented as not consuming credits; do not treat every AI operation as billable.

rows.question: Does a local MCP process keep page data local?
rows.decision: Standard analyze runs locally, with authentication/configuration traffic. Remediation sends affected HTML and violation metadata. Enabled Advanced Rules can send a full-page screenshot and required page structure/styles.
rows.boundary: Inspect the active preset before using private pages. Uploads for enabled Advanced Rules can occur even when the optional screenshot response was not requested; no network test was performed here.

rows.question: Can administrators restrict Deque AI?
rows.decision: Organisation-level AI controls and user-override permissions are documented. Private-cloud operation needs the required ML/LLM connections; on-premises private AI needs a vendor discussion.
rows.boundary: Feature availability and data-sharing controls are separate. Infrastructure may add cost; no plan-wide promise of local-only AI processing is made.

rows.question: Must Silktide AI be enabled for governance?
rows.decision: Ordinary governance remains usable without AI providers enabled. Complete documents administrative AI-provider controls; relevant AI settings are required for AI-generated analysis.
rows.boundary: Creating or accepting a recommended task does not itself edit the customer’s website. Separately permissioned AI actions and contract-specific scope must be checked.
