factual.name: Endpoint security
factual.heading: Endpoint security for US small businesses: compare protection and plan limits
factual.description: Compare Microsoft Defender, CrowdStrike, Bitdefender and Avast by endpoint scope, EDR, patching, annual costs, add-ons and documented plan boundaries.
factual.intro: Start with the laptops, desktops and phones your business actually uses. These four supplier families offer business endpoint protection, but prevention, investigation and managed response are different purchases. The table compares eight documented offers or configurations without assigning a performance score.
factual.localHeading: Build a US fleet brief before comparing prices
factual.localNote: Count people, computers, phones and servers separately. Microsoft’s small-business licence is user-based with a 300-user ceiling; CrowdStrike’s observed offers are device-priced. A server, an outsourced response team or an add-on may need another purchase. None of these comparisons establishes regulatory compliance or measured protection efficacy.
factual.checklistHeading: A short buying sequence that exposes the real scope
factual.costNote: An annual prepaid rate is not a cancellable monthly offer. The observed Microsoft amounts are monthly equivalents paid yearly; CrowdStrike’s annual amount is per device per year. Avast’s first-year amount and displayed renewal differ, and the extracted device selector and currency need confirmation. Bitdefender’s dynamic amount did not render. No cross-vendor cost winner is calculated.
buyingAdvice: Inventory operating-system versions, servers and mobile devices. Mark each as required, optional or outside scope; a platform logo does not establish identical feature parity on every OS.
Choose the operating model: prevention only, your IT team investigating alerts, or a contracted managed detection and response service. Name the person who responds outside office hours.
Require an offer-specific list for EDR, host isolation, vulnerability assessment, patch deployment, USB restrictions and web policy. Antivirus, threat hunting and backup are not interchangeable.
Before moving a fleet, run an authorised pilot for installation, exclusions, resource use, alert workflow, rollback and coexistence. This comparison has not executed that pilot.

Obtain the order’s exact currency, tax, renewal, seat floor, server cost, data-processing region, log retention and support response commitments. Do not treat a trial’s enabled modules as purchased entitlement.
migration: Record existing policies and exclusions, then export the inventory before changing agents.
Check the vendor’s supported coexistence and removal process; stage devices in a small group and retain a rollback procedure.
Verify which team receives and owns an alert, and check a documented response exercise before expanding the rollout.
factual.aiNote: Machine learning used to detect malware is different from a generative assistant or an autonomous responder. The sources document AI detection for Microsoft, CrowdStrike and Bitdefender, but do not establish comparable accuracy, prompt limits, data reuse or human-approval controls across all purchased offers. Unknown AI cells remain unknown.

categories.name: Backup and recovery
categories.description: Compare Backblaze, IDrive, Acronis and Veeam for US business computer recovery, with clear server/VM extensions, storage boundaries and plan costs.
buyingAdvice: Write a recovery brief: named computer, representative file set, maximum acceptable data loss, maximum downtime and the person authorised to restore. Separate file retrieval from booting an entire replacement machine.

Price the same inventory. Add protected computers, server workloads, SaaS seats, active data, retention growth, storage destination and required support; confirm licence conversion rules rather than equating one person to one workload.
Ask how deletions, offline laptops, disconnected external drives and exhausted capacity are handled. Retention duration and the number of retained file versions are different limits.

Design an authorised restore exercise to a clean destination. Check recovered contents, permissions, keys, bandwidth, transfer charges, application consistency and recorded recovery time. No such test has been performed for this comparison.

Document who can delete backups or change retention, how encryption keys are recovered, and whether an immutable copy is separately contracted. A version-history label does not establish immutability.

factual.name: Backup and recovery
factual.heading: Business backup and recovery: compare file protection, capacity and restore scope
factual.description: Compare Backblaze, IDrive, Acronis and Veeam for US business computer recovery, with clear server/VM extensions, storage boundaries and plan costs.
factual.intro: The common task here is recovering business files from computers after loss, deletion or an incident. All four families document that task. Acronis and Veeam also address infrastructure recovery, while Backblaze’s compared service is computer file backup. Those broader portfolios are not interchangeable packages.
factual.localHeading: Separate the computer baseline from server and cloud extensions
factual.localNote: List protected computers and the files that must be recovered first. Then add image recovery, databases, virtual machines and SaaS as separate requirements. Per-computer storage, pooled capacity and workload licences use different billing units. A successful backup job does not by itself prove that a real restore meets your recovery objectives.
factual.checklistHeading: Specify the recovery you will actually need
factual.costNote: Backblaze’s observed annual amount is per computer; IDrive’s selected monthly tiers have different pooled capacities. buyingAdvice: Write a recovery brief: named computer, representative file set, maximum acceptable data loss, maximum downtime and the person authorised to restore. Separate file retrieval from booting an entire replacement machine.

Price the same inventory. Add protected computers, server workloads, SaaS seats, active data, retention growth, storage destination and required support; confirm licence conversion rules rather than equating one person to one workload.
Ask how deletions, offline laptops, disconnected external drives and exhausted capacity are handled. Retention duration and the number of retained file versions are different limits.

Design an authorised restore exercise to a clean destination. Check recovered contents, permissions, keys, bandwidth, transfer charges, application consistency and recorded recovery time. No such test has been performed for this comparison.

Document who can delete backups or change retention, how encryption keys are recovered, and whether an immutable copy is separately contracted. A version-history label does not establish immutability.
migration: Keep the previous backup and restore credentials until the new restore exercise succeeds.
Document exclusions, retention, key ownership and any separately billed cloud or SaaS scope before moving data.
Schedule the initial upload around available bandwidth, retain the local source and verify backup completeness before decommissioning anything.
factual.aiNote: Veeam describes threat analysis of backups; Acronis assigns some malware-scan and safe-recovery capabilities to Advanced, not automatically to Backup Advanced. These are documentary statements, not independently measured detection rates. No equivalent AI capability, recovery autonomy or included assistant quota was established for all four families.

rows.question: Recover employee documents on Windows or Mac?
rows.decision: Backblaze Business Backup is the direct computer-file option; IDrive Team provides a pooled-capacity alternative.
rows.boundary: Backblaze’s computer service is not B2 object storage or a server/VM backup product; IDrive Team’s selected row is five computers and five users.

rows.question: Restore a full machine or a running server?
rows.decision: Investigate the selected Acronis/Veeam workload and the appropriate IDrive image/server option.
rows.boundary: Do not infer bare-metal or database recovery from ordinary file backup. Confirm agents, destination, operating system and licences.

rows.question: Need central SSO, legal hold and restricted restores with Backblaze?
rows.decision: Ask for the Enterprise Control upgrade.
rows.boundary: Its combined price is quoted. Ordinary Business Backup pricing does not include every enterprise control.

rows.question: Considering Veeam Essentials for a small fleet?
rows.decision: Apply the five-licence purchase minimum and the fewer-than-250-employees / up-to-50-workloads eligibility.
rows.boundary: USD 95 per licence/year implies a USD 475 minimum licence pack at observed MSRP; storage, tax, deployment and licence-to-computer conversion are not included.

rows.question: Does buying one-year history configure every Backblaze computer?
rows.decision: The one-year option has no extra storage charge, but extended history is selected for each computer. It retains modified/deleted versions while the account is in good standing.
rows.boundary: Confirm the actual policy. Longer history cannot restore data already purged; reducing history narrows what is recoverable.

rows.question: Can a disconnected external drive stay protected?
rows.decision: Directly attached supported drives follow the selected history: one-year history can retain backed-up data for up to one year disconnected. The shorter 30-day policy has a different removal window.
rows.boundary: Only already-backed-up data is retained. Native OS read/write access and drive eligibility matter; Time Machine and certain Windows removable mounts are excluded.

rows.question: How would a large Backblaze recovery be delivered?
rows.decision: The documented web ZIP path limits a restore to 500 GB with 20 active ZIP downloads. B2 and USB methods have different limits and possible charges.
rows.boundary: Do not confuse unlimited backup capacity with unlimited single-file delivery or a guaranteed recovery time. Verify current client, fees and shipping conditions.

rows.question: What does an optional private key mean during web ZIP recovery?
rows.decision: Backblaze describes sending the passphrase over encryption to its restore servers for the web/cloud ZIP path, then discarding it after use. A forgotten private key cannot be recovered by Backblaze.
rows.boundary: This statement is limited to the documented web/cloud ZIP path, not every app or B2 path. It is not a universal zero-knowledge or independent security-audit claim.

factual.name: Field service
factual.heading: Field service software for US home-service teams
factual.description: Compare Jobber, Housecall Pro, Workiz and ServiceM8 plans, users, job limits, field workflows and AI boundaries for US service businesses.
factual.intro: Start with the work between a customer enquiry and a paid job: booking, dispatch, field documentation, invoicing and repeat service. These four supplier families serve that common workflow. They are not an assessment of industrial maintenance, construction project management or every field-service product.
factual.localHeading: US buying scope: count the team and the work before comparing prices
factual.localNote: Jobber and Housecall Pro publish USD offers with sales tax extra. ServiceM8 uses monthly job allowances and unlimited users on its paid plans; its US pricing FAQ now describes Android as well as iOS. Workiz publishes named quoted packages. Payment processing, AI answering, implementation and state-specific taxes can change the total.
factual.checklistHeading: Test one realistic day before committing
factual.costNote: Annual-equivalent prices are not month-to-month offers. For the documented five-user annual scope, Jobber Connect and Housecall Pro Essentials both show USD 149/month equivalent, or USD 1,788 for twelve months before tax and extras. This is subscription arithmetic only, not a claim of equal features or total cost. ServiceM8 Growing is USD 79/month for up to 150 new jobs; Workiz needs a quote.
buyingAdvice: Write down office users, field staff, peak new jobs per month, repeat visits and the number of businesses/locations. Ask how cancelled and recurring jobs count.
Try a customer request, an estimate, approval, dispatch, a field photo/checklist, an invoice and a payment reconciliation on permitted test data. No such trial was performed for this comparison.
For a five-person team, request the five-user offer. A one-user headline, an annually prepaid equivalent and a no-commitment monthly price are three different scopes.
Check the exact QuickBooks edition, records and sync direction. Retain a manual reconciliation path; an integration label is not proof that your accounting workflow is covered.
For AI booking, define services, service area, available slots, escalation rules and prohibited promises. Review real call/message examples with the vendor before enabling autonomous actions.
migration: Export customer/job history, open estimates and unpaid invoices before migration. Check attachments and duplicate customer matching.
Reconcile the opening balance and test job-to-invoice-to-accounting flow without sending real customer messages.
Confirm staff device compatibility, offline behaviour, permission boundaries and training. Retain a fallback schedule during cutover.
factual.aiNote: Writing assistance, analytical helpers and autonomous answering are different purchases. Housecall Pro includes several helpers but charges separately for call answering. Workiz Genius Answering has documented task/language controls but remains an add-on. ServiceM8 Office Agent Pro is extra. Jobber Receptionist Companion is marked coming soon. No performance, model accuracy, data-retention or legal compliance claim is independently tested here.

factual.name: Inventory management
factual.heading: Inventory software for US small-business stock and orders
factual.description: Compare Zoho Inventory, inFlow Inventory, Cin7 Core and Finale by stock/order workflows, real plans, user and volume limits, integrations and AI boundaries.
factual.intro: This comparison covers the common small-business task of purchasing stock, keeping quantities by location and fulfilling customer orders. Advanced warehouse execution, manufacturing and ERP are extensions that need their own scope. The four supplier families are a non-exhaustive shortlist, not a ranked list.
factual.localHeading: Put purchasing, sales and stock capacity on the same buying brief
factual.localNote: Cin7 Core prices are explicitly USD before taxes for new customers; inFlow’s selected annual rates are USD. Zoho’s US edition and Finale display dollar amounts without an explicit ISO currency in the captured offer, so that uncertainty is retained. Accounting and US-channel connections still require confirmation for your accounts and transaction flow.
factual.checklistHeading: Verify a purchase-to-return workflow with your actual limits
factual.costNote: Monthly and annual caps are different: Zoho Standard shows 500 sales orders/month and 300 purchase orders/month; Cin7 Core Standard shows 6,000 sales orders/year. inFlow advertises unlimited orders but caps users and locations. Finale publishes starting prices; capacity and configured totals need a quote. Taxes, onboarding, scanners, accounting and add-ons prevent a reliable all-in cheapest calculation.
buyingAdvice: Count named users, active locations, bins, SKUs, sales orders, purchase orders, invoices, channels and seasonal peaks separately. An annual allowance does not prove a monthly peak is unrestricted.
Use one representative purchase, partial receipt, stock transfer, customer order, shipment and return in a vendor demonstration. Ask who owns corrections when stock and accounting disagree.
Match the required accounting method and landed-cost handling before importing data. Financial FIFO costing and physical lot-picking order answer different questions.

Check connector quantities and record direction for your US accounting, marketplaces and carrier accounts. A large integration catalogue does not mean unlimited paid connectors or identical sync behaviour.
For expiry-sensitive stock, request a plan-specific demonstration of lots, expiry, picking and recall evidence. A batch-tracking label alone does not establish industry compliance.
migration: Reconcile opening quantities and valuation by location; retain the original export, adjustments and document IDs.
Pilot a small SKU set with partial receipts, bundles, refunds and accounting reconciliation before cutover.
Keep scanners, labels, connector credentials, access rights and required onboarding separate in the implementation quote.
factual.aiNote: An assistant that reports on stock is not an autonomous purchasing agent. inFlow documents read-only reporting and broad access prerequisites; its lower plans still list an AI add-on. Zoho advertises MCP actions but the inspected page did not establish plan entitlements or write-approval safeguards. Cin7 ForesightAI is an add-on despite broader product marketing. No Finale AI entitlement was verified.

decisionAid.heading: Decisions that change the inventory quote

rows.question: Will a busy month fit your subscription?
rows.decision: Zoho Standard’s limits are monthly; Cin7 Core Standard’s sales allowance is annual. inFlow’s order count is unlimited but seats/locations are not.
rows.boundary: Ask separately about seasonal peaks, purchase invoices, connectors and paid extensions. No common-volume cost winner is calculated.

rows.question: Do you need a bin or a second warehouse?
rows.decision: inFlow Lite has one location without sublocations. Cin7 distinguishes stock locations from advanced warehouse functionality. Finale Growth includes mobile barcode WMS.
rows.boundary: A location count is not proof of equivalent scanning, bin control, picking or hardware. Demonstrate the required workflow in the purchased plan.

rows.question: Could physical picking change your accounting cost?
rows.decision: inFlow documents separate picking options and valuation methods. Expiry-tracked lots use FEFO for picking; accounting methods calculate financial cost.
rows.boundary: Its costing guidance warns against changing costing options when connected to QuickBooks Online or Xero. Agree the method before migration.

rows.question: Can every warehouse worker use the AI reporting assistant?
rows.decision: inFlow’s read-only assistant requires company opt-in and broad view access; location/sales-rep restrictions disable its access. It exports reports for review.
rows.boundary: Do not widen a worker’s permissions just to enable AI. The query is not exposed; check outputs, data-use terms and the plan add-on.

rows.question: Does AI marketing mean the plan includes automated purchasing?
rows.decision: Zoho documents MCP actions; Cin7 documents forecasting as an add-on. These are different capabilities and entitlements.
rows.boundary: Ask for exact actions, permissions, approval rules, quotas, costs and rollback. No safe-autonomy or forecast-accuracy test was performed.

M-Files displayed EUR rather than USD in the inspected offer. Laserfiche publishes USD annual tariffs with minimum seats. Revver displays dollar prices but its ISO currency, term and tax were not established. Obtain a US proposal before comparing total cost; no compliance certification or data-location guarantee is inferred.

A general vendor price range is not a quotation for a named configuration. Annual subtotals below exclude tax, services and other required products; they are not total ownership cost.
buyingAdvice: Specify one document journey: import an existing record, correct its metadata, send it for approval, replace a version and retrieve the audit history. Require a demonstration with your document formats.

Ask for the exact tenant region, processing locations, identity settings and contract terms for your data. A supplier offering a US location does not establish the location of your account.
Request an exit demonstration covering original files, versions, metadata, permissions and audit history. A download button or CSV export does not prove a complete portable archive.

Map document classes, permissions and retention decisions; preserve identifiers and original exports for reconciliation.
Put conversion, cleanup, connector configuration, training and any recurring support service in the implementation scope.
factual.aiNote: Extraction, conversational answers and automatic routing are different AI tasks. Use representative documents and review disputed output. Laserfiche meters operations rather than documents. Revver describes two classification/filing features as upcoming, so this comparison does not present them as available. decisionAid.heading: Document-management decisions and a focused package comparison

rows.question: DocuWare Cloud 15 or Laserfiche Professional for 15 full users?
rows.decision: Cloud 15 includes 50 GB and a configured quotation. Laserfiche Professional publishes USD 875/user/year; 15 × 875 = USD 13,125/year subscription-only, with 100 GB/user.
rows.boundary: These are different capacity and feature bundles. Tax, migration, extra modules and the DocuWare quote prevent a valid cheapest claim.

rows.question: What does the Laserfiche minimum commitment mean?
rows.decision: At the published annual unit prices, five Professional users equal USD 4,375/year; 25 Business users equal USD 27,875/year.
rows.boundary: These arithmetic subtotals omit services, taxes and other products. Do not multiply the rounded monthly display by 12 to infer the invoice.

rows.question: Can every Revver participant administer users or approvals?
rows.decision: Full user administration needs its enabled feature. Workflow participation and approval have distinct permissions; Full and Essentials may participate when configured.
rows.boundary: Do not buy a cheap participant licence and assume it can administer every process or access every file.

rows.question: Does unlimited or included AI remove usage questions?
rows.decision: Laserfiche Smart Chat is not unit-metered, but triggered or bulk AI operations can be. Revver advertises unlimited new-user Smart Suite, while release status still varies.
rows.boundary: Request concrete input, fair-use, data-processing and administrator settings. M-Files numerical allowance was not verified.

rows.question: Does DocuWare Intelligent Indexing mean advanced IDP is included?
rows.decision: No: core Indexing learns from organization-specific corrections; advanced IDP is separately priced.
rows.boundary: Specify the desired extraction and review flow. Do not transfer licensing or data-use claims between the two products.

comparison.title: DocuWare vs Laserfiche: document workflows, licences and annual cost
comparison.description: Compare DocuWare Cloud 4/15 with Laserfiche Professional/Business: user minimums, storage, records controls, AI units and implementation gaps.
comparison.intro: Both families support organizational document capture and controlled workflows. The purchase decision is whether a quoted user/storage bundle or a published per-user plan better matches your permissions, records obligations and growth. This page compares selected cloud offers; it does not declare a score winner or assume that equivalent feature names mean identical deployment results.

choices.heading: Shortlist DocuWare for a configured bundle
choices.text: Cloud 4 includes four users and 20 GB; Cloud 15 includes 15 users and 50 GB. Core document workflow is shared across the bundles. Request a quote with the actual user mix, storage growth, implementation and optional modules. SAP, digital signatures and advanced IDP are not inferred from the shared core.

choices.heading: Shortlist Laserfiche when published plan boundaries help budgeting
choices.text: Professional has a five-user minimum; Business has a 25-user minimum and adds records controls and higher capacity. Professional optional records/audit scope needs its own quote. A smaller team should not compare a single Business seat with a complete DocuWare package.

decisionAid.heading: A 15-person document team: what can actually be priced?

rows.question: Subscription boundary
rows.decision: DocuWare Cloud 15 has 15 users and 50 GB but no executable public package price. Fifteen Laserfiche Professional users at USD 875/user/year equal USD 13,125/year for the subscription.
rows.boundary: The workflows and storage units differ. This is not an all-in cost comparison or a lowest-price recommendation; tax, implementation, modules and usage remain outside the subtotal.

rows.question: Would Business solve a records requirement?
rows.decision: The published Laserfiche Business minimum is 25 users: 25 × USD 1,115/year = USD 27,875/year before extras. A 15-person team still needs to account for that minimum if choosing this offer.
rows.boundary: Confirm whether Professional plus a records add-on or a configured DocuWare solution meets the actual requirement. No compliance conclusion follows from a product label.

rows.question: Will document AI create a second bill?
rows.decision: DocuWare Intelligent Indexing is distinct from separately scoped advanced IDP. Laserfiche publishes 1,000 annual AI units for Professional and 50,000 for Business; units are operation-based, not a document allowance.
rows.boundary: Use representative documents to obtain a workload estimate. Numeric DocuWare processing rights and Laserfiche overage costs are not settled here. No processing test was run.

buyingAdvice: Use an employee laptop or VPN request as a common demonstration: submit it, find the relevant article, route it, apply an SLA, link the asset and approve a change. This proposed scenario has not been executed by System Compare.
Distinguish incident handling, root-cause problem management and approved change. A portal with ticket routing does not prove that every ITIL-style workflow is included in the entry plan.

factual.intro: A procurement system must move a purchase from request to approval, supplier order, delivery and an invoice finance can reconcile. These four supplier families address that related workflow, but their entry prices include different modules and user roles. Compare the configured process and its exceptions before choosing a package. Ratings remain pending.
factual.localHeading: Build a US finance brief around entities, suppliers and accounting

Record the accounting edition, vendor onboarding requirements, approval limits and whether payment execution is actually in scope. ProcureDesk Growth explicitly describes EIN/W-9 collection; Procurify documents US payment options, whose eligibility and fees still need agreement. Neither a tax-form field nor a payment integration proves tax compliance or access to a payment service.
factual.checklistHeading: A procurement acceptance checklist
factual.costNote: Compare first-year and renewal totals for the same users, entities, modules and connectors. Precoro prices are annual starting rates in USD. Tradogram and ProcureDesk use dollar symbols with unresolved currency codes in this evidence. Procurify configurations require quotes. Include setup, document capture, payments and exit work without assigning zero to unknown charges.
buyingAdvice: Trace one request through approval, supplier order, partial delivery, invoice matching and accounting. Identify the system of record at every handoff.
Ask which requests, receipts, budget controls and AP functions are included in the named plan versus paid modules.
Count requester, receiver, approver, purchasing and AP roles separately. A free requester is not necessarily a free buyer or administrator.

categories.description: Compare Perplexity, Elicit, Consensus and Scite by research workflow, documented plans, citations, exports and buying limits.
buyingAdvice: Define one repeatable research question, source corpus, date cutoff and output. Record whether open-web freshness, a controlled paper set or citation monitoring drives the purchase.
Inspect supporting passages and source rights. A system can summarize an abstract without having access to the full methods or results.
Measure your own workflow in the supplier’s units: reports, messages, table columns, paper counts or connector credits. Keep API and web-app charges separate.
Confirm exact plan exports and collaboration rights. Elicit report exports are available on all plans, while Agent table exports start at Plus and Systematic Review exports require Pro or above.
Record original currency, first-year payable amount, tax and renewal. Ask for clarification where the public page has inconsistent variants or cancellation language.
Assign a human source checker and an owner for uploaded material. Source-linked answers and training exclusions do not establish accuracy or a complete privacy outcome.

factual.name: AI search & research
factual.heading: AI search and research tools for US teams
factual.description: Compare Perplexity, Elicit, Consensus and Scite by research workflow, documented plans, citations, exports and buying limits.
factual.intro: Choose what you need to research before choosing an AI subscription. Web investigation, structured extraction, scientific-paper synthesis and citation monitoring overlap, but they do not have interchangeable source coverage. This comparison covers four supplier families and eight actual offers; it does not rank them by the size of their feature lists.
factual.localHeading: US buying context: invoice, access and document controls
factual.localNote: A public dollar price is not a completed US purchase. Perplexity documents USD as the base web currency; Scite’s terms identify USD unless checkout specifies otherwise. Consensus’s inspected help page shows $ without a currency code, so we leave that code unverified. Elicit’s applicable Pro segment and amount remain unresolved. Confirm the billing address, sales tax, recurring commitment, institutional entitlement and permission to upload source material. No supplier account or regional checkout was tested.
factual.checklistHeading: Build a research buying brief
factual.costNote: Separate human seats, reports, source resources, API calls and MCP credits. Free, quote-only and a price we could not verify are different states. A monthly-equivalent annual price does not mean you can cancel after one month.
buyingAdvice: Define one repeatable research question, source corpus, date cutoff and output. Record whether open-web freshness, a controlled paper set or citation monitoring drives the purchase.
Inspect supporting passages and source rights. A system can summarize an abstract without having access to the full methods or results.
Measure your own workflow in the supplier’s units: reports, messages, table columns, paper counts or connector credits. Keep API and web-app charges separate.
Confirm exact plan exports and collaboration rights. Elicit report exports are available on all plans, while Agent table exports start at Plus and Systematic Review exports require Pro or above.
Record original currency, first-year payable amount, tax and renewal. Ask for clarification where the public page has inconsistent variants or cancellation language.
Assign a human source checker and an owner for uploaded material. Source-linked answers and training exclusions do not establish accuracy or a complete privacy outcome.
migration: Export references with identifiers, notes and the search date. Test that the receiving reference manager keeps the needed metadata.
Save the original prompt, filters and source list before moving projects. A fresh query may return a different corpus.

For Elicit sessions created before 30 September 2026, the documentation says legacy exports remain available and sessions will be removed on an unspecified date in 2027; export or migrate anything needed.
Keep organizational credentials, cancellation dates and API keys with an accountable owner; verify deletion and recurring charges separately.
factual.aiNote: Our review inspected official documentation, not answer accuracy. Use a repeatable exercise containing a known source, a conflicting finding and a correction. Inspect unsupported conclusions, missing citations and actual access to full text. Pending /100 means no editorial rating has been assigned; it is not a zero or an evidence-count percentage.

decisionAid.heading: Choose a workflow before comparing a price

rows.question: A business analyst needs current web sources
rows.decision: Perplexity is a web-first research option. Elicit Research Agent also reaches the web alongside academic papers.
rows.boundary: Use the same dated question and open the actual sources. Neither a cited response nor a model choice proves that the answer is correct.

rows.question: A researcher must screen and extract from a defined paper set
rows.decision: Elicit Pro adds a controlled Systematic Review workflow. Basic still has Research Agent and reports; Agent table exports begin at Plus.
rows.boundary: A generated PRISMA-style report does not establish review completeness. Check search strings, excluded papers, extraction quotations and the exact export entitlement.

rows.question: A writer needs cited scientific answers or follow-up citation monitoring
rows.decision: Consensus provides paper synthesis with inspectable passages. Scite focuses on how papers are cited, with alerts and supporting/contrasting/mentioning context.
rows.boundary: Abstract-based results, full-text access and citation classifications have different limits. Do not use a citation label as an independent verdict on a study.

rows.question: An assistant integration will make 600 calls in a month
rows.decision: Consensus Pro includes 500 shared API/MCP calls; its documented opt-in ceiling is 1,000. An illustrative extra 100 calls at the displayed $0.05 is $5 before tax, with currency unverified.
rows.boundary: This assumes each call processes no more than 100 papers and extra usage is enabled. Scite MCP credits use a different unit; Perplexity web Pro excludes API billing.

rows.question: Confidential documents or team administration are involved
rows.decision: Scite documents a Customer Data training exclusion. Perplexity individual Pro has an opt-out setting; its Enterprise terms are different.
rows.boundary: A training exclusion is not a retention, residency or access guarantee. Confirm the actual contract, model providers, deletion process and team tier before upload.

comparison.title: Consensus Pro vs Scite Basic: research answers or citation context?
comparison.description: Compare documented research, citation, quota and billing boundaries for Consensus Pro and Scite Basic in a US buying context.
comparison.intro: Both tools help a reader work from scientific sources. Consensus Pro is a candidate for question-led synthesis; Scite Basic is a candidate for inspecting and monitoring citation context. These are researched offers with pending ratings, not an accuracy contest.

choices.heading: Choose Consensus Pro when question-led synthesis is the main job
choices.text: Pro combines unlimited Pro messages with 15 Deep reviews each month and 500 shared API/MCP calls. The citation interface lets readers inspect supporting passages and distinguish full-text use from abstract or metadata use. This helps source checking; it does not replace it.

choices.heading: Choose Scite Basic when citation context and alerts matter more
choices.text: Basic includes Assistant and Search, article Smart Citation reports, citation alerts and collections of up to 1,000 papers. Its 250 MCP credits are not asserted to equal 250 questions. API access belongs to Pro; a buyer needing programmatic work should compare that different offer.

choices.heading: Similar displayed monthly numbers do not establish equal annual costs
choices.text: Consensus lists $144 for an annual Pro subscription, shown as $12 per month; its help article does not identify the currency code. Scite displays USD 12 per month with annual billing selected, but we did not inspect the final annual charge. Confirm currency, sales tax, renewal and the trial cancellation cutoff before deciding on price.

factual.intro: Choose the training workflow before comparing the subscription. Employee onboarding, customer academies and multi-audience learning need different permission, reporting and integration rules. These seven offers are documented, unranked starting points; no hands-on learning test or final score is recorded.
factual.localHeading: Start with the US learner population and training data
factual.localNote: Count employees, contractors, customer learners and administrators separately. A created account can be billable even if its owner never logs in. LearnUpon explicitly excludes uses requiring HIPAA-compliant handling of health or sensitive personal data within its LMS; do not upload such records on the strength of a general LMS claim. Absorb has a US contact route, but we have not tested local support or reviewed your contract. Accessibility, storage location and organizational training obligations require separate evidence.
factual.checklistHeading: Build a like-for-like LMS request
factual.costNote: Quote the same enabled/registered/monthly-active population and the same term. Record modules, setup, support, tax and renewals separately. TalentLMS publishes USD; the ISO currency behind 360Learning’s dollar symbol was not independently established in this review.

rows.question: Which learners are billable?

factual.name: Invoicing
factual.heading: Invoicing software for US small businesses
factual.description: Compare Zoho Invoice, FreshBooks, Invoice Ninja and Square by real plans, invoice/client limits, renewal costs and separate payment charges.
factual.intro: For a small business, the right invoice system depends on clients, documents, collaborators and how customers pay. This comparison keeps free software, paid bookkeeping packages and payments-connected invoices distinct. Network e-invoicing is a separate requirement, linked below.
factual.localHeading: Keep records and payment costs separate from the invoice subscription
factual.localNote: The IRS describes business records and supporting documents needed to show income and expenses; a software listing does not certify your recordkeeping or tax position. Keep exportable copies and ask your accountant what your business must retain. Card and ACH charges can exceed a small subscription, while sales-tax calculation is separate from nexus assessment and filing. A customer or agency asking for structured delivery needs the exact network or submission instructions.
factual.checklistHeading: Model the full invoicing workload
factual.costNote: Use regular renewal prices and the same number of clients, locations and users. Add gateway fees, optional advanced payments, tax and extra staff. Invoice Ninja’s displayed dollar amounts retain an unverified currency code; they are not converted or declared cheapest.
buyingAdvice: Count annual invoices, active billable clients, simultaneous projects and collaborating staff.
Separate a subscription promotion from its regular renewal and cancellation terms.
Run deposit, partial payment, credit and overdue scenarios before migrating.
Confirm how gateway settlements reconcile to the invoice and bank record.
Treat Peppol, DBNAlliance and agency portals as distinct from sending an invoice email.
migration: Export invoices, customer records, attachments and outstanding balances from the old system.
Reconcile open invoices and recurring schedules so migration does not duplicate a charge.
Keep records outside an inactive free account and test recovery before cancelling access.
factual.aiNote: Receipt capture and AI contract clauses require review of amounts, parties and terms. A vendor’s automation claim does not establish autonomous accounting accuracy. No invoice was issued, payment taken or AI output tested in this research.

rows.question: Can free invoicing support my workload?
rows.decision: Zoho Invoice documents two users, three projects and 500 invoices/year. Square Free has no monthly subscription but payment processing fees.

rows.question: What will I pay after an introductory offer?

rows.boundary: Budget regular renewal, extra staff and payment services separately.

rows.question: Do I need multiple milestones or batch invoices?
rows.decision: Square Plus adds milestone payment schedules, custom templates and batch invoices beyond Free.
rows.boundary: Its USD 49 fee is per location, with separate processing charges.

rows.question: Will emailed invoices meet a network request?
rows.decision: Invoice Ninja Enterprise documents Peppol through Storecove with 250 credits; the other tables do not establish that transport.

factual.name: E-invoicing
factual.heading: E-invoicing networks and integration for US businesses
factual.description: Compare four DBNAlliance-listed provider families for structured invoices, ERP integration and documented scope, with IPP as a separate federal-agency route.
factual.intro: A structured invoice is data exchanged through an agreed format and route. It is not simply an emailed PDF. Start with the recipient’s requirement: a business exchange network, a cross-border format or a federal-agency submission process. This page compares configured services without inventing a universal US deadline or a compliance winner.
factual.localHeading: Check the agency route before buying a network connector
factual.localNote: IPP is a Treasury service available at no charge to vendors of participating federal agencies; enrollment follows the relevant agency process. It is a useful benchmark, not a fifth paid supplier. DBNAlliance separately lists all four providers below as certified service providers. That listing establishes the network-body status observed today, not acceptance by every buyer, IPP access or a legal requirement covering every US business.
factual.checklistHeading: Define a transport and acceptance contract
factual.costNote: No numerical price was verified for these four configured offerings. Request the same outbound/inbound volumes, legal entities, networks, countries, connectors and archive period. Quote-only is not free, and unrelated sales-tax subscriptions are not prices for e-invoicing.
buyingAdvice: Obtain recipient identifiers, required format, network and acceptance status definitions in writing.
Distinguish a message being delivered from an invoice accepted for processing or approved for payment.
Name the party responsible for ERP mapping, counterparty onboarding and exception handling.
Specify audit export, retention location, portability, support hours and outage escalation.
Use agency instructions for federal invoices rather than assuming a network certification grants access.
migration: Inventory trading-party identifiers and existing endpoint registrations before changing providers.
Retain originals, responses and references needed to reconcile old invoices after the switch.
Agree a cutover window and replay/idempotency policy so the same invoice is not sent twice.
factual.aiNote: The documented AI monitoring claim is not evidence that an assistant may independently approve, alter or send invoices. Keep monetary changes and transmission permissions under explicit controls. AI extraction, model data use and autonomous-action limits remain unverified where shown.

factual.heading: AI agents and automation for US business workflows
factual.description: Compare Zapier, Make, n8n and Workato by action controls, real usage units, migration boundaries and seven documented offers. Ratings are pending.
factual.intro: Start with a bounded business action: draft a record, retrieve an answer or propose an update for approval. These platforms can connect AI to operational systems, but their billing and permission models differ. The comparison documents seven offers without claiming an autonomous agent has been tested or ranking them by unverified outcomes.
factual.localHeading: Define the business action, account permissions and US purchasing terms
factual.localNote: A US team can evaluate public paid workflows or a configured enterprise contract, but the quote must name the billing unit and model route. Workato lists a US data center; its model-routing qualification is not a guarantee that every inference stays in the US. n8n prices observed here remain in EUR. Tax, response-time commitments and most data-retention periods were not established. Restrict customer-data access and external writes until a responsible owner approves the intended action.
factual.checklistHeading: Scope one controlled agent workflow
factual.costNote: A Zapier task, Make credit, n8n execution and Workato Genie action are not interchangeable. Use the same model, successful tool calls, retries and monthly workload. Keep provider token charges, setup, tax and the committed term separate. Make prices remain unverified; Workato requires a configured quote.

decisionAid.heading: Questions that change the agent shortlist

rows.question: What is the billing unit?
rows.decision: Zapier multiplies a base step plus successful tool calls by model tier. Make combines operations and model tokens. n8n charges workflow executions.
rows.boundary: One agent conversation is not a common unit. Run the same bounded scenario before comparing cost.

rows.question: Can the agent make an external change unattended?
rows.decision: Zapier offers per-tool approval but leaves it off by default. n8n can route specified tool calls to an approve/deny step. Workato limits Genies to assigned skills.
rows.boundary: A prompt saying ask first is not the same as an enforced approval gate. No action was executed in this review.

rows.question: Will a migrated agent behave the same?
rows.decision: Zapier documents migration gaps in knowledge connectors, agent delegation and on-demand chat. Make AI Agents New remains in open beta.
rows.boundary: Keep an old and new workflow from both writing the same record during cutover. Beta status is a deployment consideration, not a measured failure rate.

rows.question: Does an enterprise agent have one flat fee?
rows.decision: Workato counts a user input as a Genie action; internal reasoning and skills are included, while some Tasks, Pages and Events can be separate.
rows.boundary: Contract enablement and the quoted services still determine cost. No public numerical Agent Studio price was established.

factual.description: Compare Notion, ClickUp, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Google Workspace by plan entitlements, AI allowances, permission boundaries and real suite costs.
factual.intro: Document workspaces and full office suites solve overlapping tasks, but they are not identical replacements. Start with the files, messages and work records your team already uses. These eight offers describe documented capabilities and limitations; no answer-quality benchmark or final editorial score has been recorded.
factual.localHeading: Match the US contract to the existing suite and data boundary
factual.localNote: Microsoft’s selected offers include the underlying business suite and Copilot. Google’s US pricing documentation distinguishes annual commitment from flexible billing; invoice timing still depends on the purchase path. Both business ranges have a 300-user ceiling. Notion returned localized non-US prices, so its US amount remains unverified. Permission-aware retrieval does not fix overly broad source permissions: review who can access sensitive files before introducing a workplace assistant.
factual.checklistHeading: Compare the knowledge workflow and total suite cost
factual.costNote: Price the same users, term, storage and required security controls. Do not add a base license twice to a complete Copilot bundle. Separate recurring AI allowance, extra credits and metered agents. ClickUp’s regular dollar amount is shown without asserting an unverified currency code; taxes are not verified.

decisionAid.heading: Questions that change the office shortlist

rows.question: Am I buying the assistant or the whole suite?
rows.decision: The Microsoft offers below are Business Standard/Premium with Copilot bundles. Google Standard/Plus are Workspace editions.
rows.boundary: Do not add a second base-suite subscription to an already complete bundle. Confirm the exact SKU on renewal.

rows.question: Do more credits mean more premium chat?
rows.decision: ClickUp AI Credits fund agents, automations and related work. Premium Brain model allowance is a separate limit. Notion separates Standard, Select and paid workspace credits.
rows.boundary: Do not translate credits into a fixed count of questions. Usage complexity, model and commercial agreement can change consumption.

rows.question: Does no training mean no retention?
rows.decision: Microsoft says prompts, responses and Graph data do not train foundation LLMs but retains interaction history. Notion Business providers can retain inputs for up to 30 days.
rows.boundary: Notion Enterprise has model exceptions to zero retention; owners can opt into those models. Check storage, provider retention and training separately.

rows.question: Which controls change between office editions?
rows.decision: Google Plus adds Vault and advanced endpoint controls beyond Standard. Microsoft Premium adds stronger identity and device/data protections.
rows.boundary: These are documented entitlements, not a security audit or proof that a deployment has configured them correctly.

factual.name: AI meetings & communications
factual.heading: AI meeting assistants for US teams
factual.description: Compare Otter, Fireflies, Fathom and tl;dv across eight real offers, meeting limits, AI charges, recording controls and data-use boundaries.
factual.intro: A meeting assistant should produce a usable record without capturing more than the team intends. Compare live minutes, file imports, stored history and AI questions separately. These eight documented offers are not ranked by transcription accuracy: no live meeting, recording upload or model-output test was performed.
factual.localHeading: Agree recording rules and data use before enabling a bot
factual.localNote: US teams may have participants in different locations and contractual settings. Review your organization’s recording and notice requirements rather than treating a visible bot as sufficient permission. Otter states participant-consent and notice requirements; tl;dv describes automatic calendar rules and optional disclosure email. Keep supplier training, subprocessor training, storage and deletion policies separate. Fathom in this comparison is the meeting assistant, not Fathom Analytics.
factual.checklistHeading: Define a representative meeting workload
factual.costNote: Use the same user count and meeting workload, but keep monthly subscriptions distinct from annual monthly equivalents. Fathom requires at least two paid users. Fireflies initial AI credits are a one-time team allowance and can lead to a separate subscription. Current tl;dv prices and several dollar currency codes were not verified.

migration: Export recordings, transcripts and important corrections before cancelling an existing account.
Review calendar integrations so two assistants do not join the same meeting automatically.

factual.aiNote: A fluent summary can misattribute a decision or action owner. Compare generated text with the recording and require a person to approve external CRM updates. No vendor transcription accuracy percentage or coaching score is treated as an independent benchmark in this review.

decisionAid.heading: Questions that change the meeting shortlist

rows.question: What does unlimited recording cover?
rows.decision: Otter Business has unlimited in-app minutes but a 6,000-minute monthly imported-file allowance per user. Fireflies separates transcription from stored minutes and advanced AI credits.
rows.boundary: Unlimited file count, stored history, live minutes and AI questions are different limits.

rows.question: Can AI usage create an extra subscription?
rows.decision: Fireflies describes one-time initial team credits and an automatic monthly credit subscription after their exhaustion on a paid plan.
rows.boundary: Review the current billing controls before importing a large call library. Initial credits are not a monthly per-seat allowance.

rows.question: Can recordings be used for training?
rows.decision: Otter describes proprietary training with de-identified data. Fathom offers an opt-out from its own model improvement. Fireflies and tl;dv state no-training defaults.
rows.boundary: A prohibition on third-party model training does not necessarily prohibit the recording supplier from improving its own models.

rows.question: Should I enable automatic recording for every meeting?
rows.decision: Otter requires participant consent and notice. tl;dv documents calendar defaults and an optional attendee disclosure email.
rows.boundary: Choose recording rules with your organization before rollout. These vendor statements are not legal advice or a determination of consent requirements for a particular call.

factual.name: AI writing & language
factual.heading: AI writing and language tools for US teams
factual.description: Compare Grammarly, QuillBot, ProWritingAid and Wordtune using eight actual offers, writing limits, data-use defaults and explicit price uncertainty.
factual.intro: Choose the writing workflow before the subscription: everyday business editing, paraphrasing and summaries, or long-form English revision. These four specialist products have different quotas and data defaults. The comparison records eight offers and their documented limitations without treating a detector result as proof of authorship or claiming that generated wording has been independently tested.
factual.localHeading: US English, procurement route and confidential text
factual.localNote: ProWritingAid explicitly supports a US-English setting, while exact dialect controls were not established for every other offer. Grammarly’s selected Pro price is in USD; QuillBot Team returned EUR and is left in that currency. ProWritingAid and Wordtune displayed dollar symbols without an independently established ISO currency. Tax and most support response commitments remain unknown. decisionAid.heading: Questions that change a writing shortlist

rows.question: Does buying a paid plan disable training?
rows.decision: Grammarly website-purchased Pro begins with training enabled, while its Enterprise default differs. QuillBot excludes Team inputs from training.
rows.boundary: Check the actual purchasing route and account setting; a paid subscription alone is not a universal no-training commitment.

rows.question: Are these all-purpose writing tools?
rows.decision: ProWritingAid supports US English and long-form editing; it currently supports English only. Wordtune emphasizes rewrites and summaries.
rows.boundary: A story critique, a grammar suggestion and a document summary answer different needs. No writing-quality ranking has been measured.

rows.question: What is the actual allowance?
rows.decision: QuillBot Premium limits plagiarism checks to 25,000 words/month. Wordtune Advanced separates 30 daily rewrites from 15 monthly summaries.
rows.boundary: An unlimited label for one function does not remove another function’s quota.

rows.question: Is text deleted after every check?
rows.decision: ProWritingAid describes removing analyzed text after processing, but saved Web Editor documents are retained. Wordtune has deletion-request and retention exceptions.
rows.boundary: Processing, saved documents and training are separate questions. Do not infer zero retention from no training.

factual.name: AI software development
factual.heading: AI coding tools and agents for US development teams
factual.description: Compare GitHub Copilot, Cursor, JetBrains AI/Junie and Augment Code by actual subscriptions, code-data settings, editor coverage and usage units.
factual.intro: An inline coding assistant, a cloud agent and a pull-request reviewer affect different parts of development. Start with the repository, editor and review process the team actually uses. This comparison documents eight offers across four suppliers, while keeping individual licenses distinct from organization contracts. No benchmark, code execution or security outcome has been measured for these products.
factual.localHeading: Match the US buying entity to the developer workflow
factual.localNote: JetBrains explicitly lists the United States as an eligible AI territory; its individual prices are distinct from organization and pooled Central billing. GitHub Pro and Pro+ below are individual plans. Cursor Teams/Enterprise and Augment Standard/Business describe team purchasing. US tax is not assumed included; Cursor explicitly excludes applicable taxes. Actual processing regions, contract warranties and model retention remain unverified where the source packet does not establish them.
factual.checklistHeading: Specify one coding workflow and its control boundary
factual.costNote: Do not equate GitHub AI Credits, JetBrains AI Credits, Cursor usage or Augment dollar-based consumption. decisionAid.heading: Questions that change the coding shortlist

rows.question: Is this a seat fee or a team balance?
rows.decision: Augment Standard/Business are flat monthly team plans for up to 50 seats. GitHub’s selected plans are individual subscriptions; Cursor Teams is priced per user.
rows.boundary: An included usage balance is not an unlimited compute allowance or a cash credit against another vendor.

rows.question: Do credits cover every model?
rows.decision: Cursor’s current pricing bills third-party models separately at API list price. GitHub and JetBrains use their own AI-credit allowances.
rows.boundary: Credits and model multipliers cannot be converted into a common count of finished coding tasks.

rows.question: Is company code excluded from training?
rows.decision: GitHub individual users can opt out. Cursor requires Privacy Mode. JetBrains detailed code collection is opt-in. Augment excludes paid-plan data.
rows.boundary: These statements concern training; they do not establish identical processing location or retention.

rows.question: Does an IDE integration support every feature?
rows.decision: JetBrains publishes a per-IDE matrix; diagnostics are not identical across all IDEs. GitHub also supports multiple editor surfaces.
rows.boundary: Demonstrate the exact editor, version and workflow before transferring a trial result to the whole team.

factual.name: AI app & website building
factual.heading: AI app and website builders for US teams
factual.description: Compare Lovable, Replit, Bolt and v0 across actual plans, hosting limits, collaboration, source portability and AI-data defaults.
factual.intro: A working preview is the start of an application decision, not proof that a production system is ready. Compare how code is edited, who can collaborate, how hosting is billed and what remains portable. These eight offers expose differences between shared workspace credits, per-member tokens and metered deployment. They do not promise a production-ready or secure application from one prompt.
factual.localHeading: Budget a US production workload beyond the first build
factual.localNote: Lovable documents entry monthly tiers in USD. v0 also identifies USD and adds applicable tax according to billing address, but its Plus offer has an unresolved renewal price. Bolt’s displayed dollar ISO code was not established. Replit’s numeric fees could not be read reliably from the live pricing page. For customer-facing US work, document domain ownership, the operator responsible for support and the handling of customer data before connecting production credentials.
factual.checklistHeading: Compare the whole build-to-operation path
factual.costNote: Separate build generation, runtime AI, database storage, network requests and additional services. A seat is not a concurrent task; an unlimited number of published apps is not unlimited hosting consumption. Treat v0 Plus as an observed promotion and ask for the regular renewal amount.
buyingAdvice: Define the smallest application and the real users who will access it.
Check whether source code, data and domain ownership can leave the platform.
Keep preview access distinct from production authentication.
Inspect credits, automatic top-ups and expected hosting traffic before public launch.
Review generated code and permissions using synthetic data before adding real customer records.
migration: Export source and data and document every external service credential.
Verify rollback and database recovery independently; a source-code restore may not restore user data.
Test domain cutover and access controls before retiring the existing application.
factual.aiNote: No supplier account, generated application, payment or deployment was tested. Vendor security tools are documented controls rather than an independent security assessment. Ratings remain pending /100; missing portability, tax, privacy and runtime-cost details remain explicit.

decisionAid.heading: Questions that change an app-builder shortlist

rows.question: Are team credits pooled?
rows.decision: Lovable uses workspace credits. Replit Pro pools workspace credits across up to 15 builders. Bolt gives each paid team member a separate token allowance.
rows.boundary: Seat count, simultaneous tasks and shared budget are different limits.

rows.question: Does the subscription cover production hosting?
rows.decision: Lovable meters Cloud and runtime AI alongside building. Replit credits pay for several services. Bolt Pro lists a web-request allowance.
rows.boundary: Do not compare one prompt with one hosted-app month. Ask separately about database storage, traffic and runtime inference.

rows.question: When is source material excluded from training?
rows.decision: Lovable Business excludes workspace data by default; Pro needs account opt-out. Bolt’s Team exclusion requires an MSA or DPA. v0 Business lists opt-out by default.
rows.boundary: The v0 AI policy uses Vercel hosting plan names; it does not establish the current Plus default.

rows.question: Is the displayed monthly figure stable?
rows.decision: v0 Plus shows USD 30 with USD 90 crossed out. Replit’s live plan cards were not readable in this research.

factual.name: LLM observability & evaluation
factual.heading: LLM observability and evaluation for US engineering teams
factual.description: Compare LangSmith, Langfuse, Braintrust and Arize AX across eight offers, trace billing, evaluation scope, retention and US procurement.
factual.intro: Instrument a production workflow before choosing its evaluation dashboard. These four supplier families cover overlapping trace and evaluation tasks, but bill different units and attach different rights to their entry plans. A span allowance is not a request allowance, and a retained trace is not the same thing as an accessible dataset. This comparison keeps product documentation separate from selected-plan entitlements and leaves untested evaluation quality unrated.
factual.localHeading: US billing, regions and the production-data agreement
factual.localNote: Arize’s terms describe USD billing and US-bank-issued cards, with an invoicing fallback; the card wording is relevant to the purchasing route rather than a reason to exclude a US customer. Its Free and Pro plan table lists US, EU and Canada regions. Langfuse lists Oregon, Ireland and Japan. LangSmith separates US and EU services, including a US-only Tuned Evaluators beta. Braintrust’s selected-plan region remains unresolved. A region label alone does not settle all processing, retention or contractual requirements.
factual.checklistHeading: Trace, evaluation and retention checks that change the bill
factual.costNote: Budget seats or platform fees, captured units, evaluator/model usage, storage, retention extensions and administration add-ons separately. Exact Arize overages remain unresolved because storage and ingestion terminology differs across pages. Applicable taxes are additional where documented; no final checkout was performed.
buyingAdvice: Choose one application boundary: request, multi-turn session and nested tool calls.
Estimate daily traffic and peak trace size before comparing included units.

migration: Export a small approved trace and its evaluation result before replacing the current system.
Keep the application request ID stable while instrumenting the new SDK or OpenTelemetry path.
Verify deletion of traces independently from datasets, audit records and access windows.
factual.aiNote: No accounts, production traces or evaluation benchmarks were run. Automated judges can disagree with a human rubric. A documented feature or lower platform fee does not establish better evaluation accuracy; ratings remain pending /100.

comparison.title: LangSmith vs Langfuse: trace billing, retention and evaluation scope
comparison.description: A stored comparison of Developer/Plus and Core/Pro, with plan-level evidence and unresolved rights.
comparison.intro: Both products document tracing and evaluation, but their metering, retention and administration boundaries differ. Compare an application workload and a data-handling contract rather than choosing by the first monthly number.

choices.heading: Consider LangSmith for its tracing and experiment workflow
choices.text: Developer and Plus have different seat economics, and extra usage can exceed the entry fee. Decide which traces need extended retention. The US-only Tuned Evaluators beta is a region and offer question, not a universal entitlement.

choices.heading: Consider Langfuse when hosted controls and operational choice matter
choices.text: Core and Pro are hosted subscriptions; self-hosting has separate infrastructure and staffing costs. Pro’s Teams add-on is distinct from base Pro, and the stated access window must not be presented as a deletion policy.

factual.name: AI-assisted mechanical CAD
factual.heading: Mechanical CAD and engineering AI for US teams
factual.description: Compare Fusion, Onshape, SOLIDWORKS Design Offer and Siemens Designcenter X through eight commercial offers, US costs and engineering limits.
factual.intro: This category compares mechanical-part design, assemblies and engineering documentation. It does not combine building BIM, factory controls, clinical design or generic 3D image generation into one ranking. Start with the part and release workflow, then establish which simulation, manufacturing and AI functions belong to the selected commercial offer. An AI assistant’s presence is not evidence that an exported drawing or manufactured part is correct.
factual.localHeading: US offer, named seats and confidential designs
factual.localNote: SOLIDWORKS explicitly publishes USA prices for its named-user Design Offer: Standard $2,820 and Professional $3,456 per year before local tax. Onshape’s USD selector lists $1,500 and $2,500 per user/year for Standard and Professional. Fusion’s US page advertises $57/month billed annually; the annual invoice and tax were not captured, so no total is derived from that rounded display. Siemens store responses expose offer names but no usable US amount. These prices do not establish suitability for regulated or export-controlled work.
factual.checklistHeading: Check the mechanical workflow before adding AI
factual.costNote: Separate named-user licenses, data management, manufacturing or simulation bundles, AI credits and shared token pools. SOLIDWORKS Blue Tokens and Siemens reusable Value Based Licensing tokens are different mechanisms. Confirm renewal, expiration and concurrent-use behavior before estimating total cost.
buyingAdvice: Use a representative part, assembly and drawing as acceptance material.
Specify commercial/private-data requirements before considering a free offer.
Check whether simulation, CAM and release management are base functions or higher-tier rights.
Ask for the exact current SKU and a tax-inclusive US quote.
Require an engineer to validate geometry, tolerances and manufacturing output.
migration: Export native files and neutral formats with a known drawing revision.
Test relationships, configurations, units and custom properties after import.
Keep release history and approval records separate from a successful geometry import.
factual.aiNote: No CAD account, file conversion, simulation, manufacturing or AI accuracy test was performed. AI capabilities are documentary observations. Ratings remain pending /100, and unresolved AI rollout, license scope and data-processing details remain explicit.

rows.decision: Onshape Free is public and non-commercial; Standard and Professional are private commercial offers.

guide.title: How to compare mechanical CAD offers, AI credits and engineering risk

comparison.title: Onshape vs SOLIDWORKS Design Offer: private CAD, team control and US annual cost
comparison.description: A stored comparison of two Standard and Professional offer pairs, with named-user pricing and documentary limitations.
comparison.intro: These offers overlap in mechanical CAD but use different application and collaboration models. Compare the exact private commercial workflow, release needs and license identity before choosing by annual cost.

choices.heading: Consider Onshape when browser-based team data is central
choices.text: Standard is private commercial CAD; Professional adds company data and release capabilities. The documented annual USD tariffs are $1,500 and $2,500 per user. A public Free document is not a substitute for a private commercial design, and Government Enterprise is separate.

choices.heading: Consider the SOLIDWORKS Design Offer for a local CAD application with connected data
choices.text: The single named-user US Standard/Professional offers are $2,820/$3,456 per year excluding local tax. The Professional offer adds tools such as rendering and costing. Confirm that the quote is this offer rather than a device-locked license and establish the AI token allowance separately.

demo: Use an authorized mechanical part with dimensional constraints.
Import or rebuild an assembly, then change one component and inspect its drawing.
Compare required release and reviewer permissions on the exact offer.
Export a neutral file and inspect units, geometry and custom properties.
Have an engineer approve the result; do not treat an assistant answer as a released design.

factual.heading: AI marketing and creative tools for US campaign teams
factual.description: Compare Jasper, Copy.ai, Anyword and AdCreative.ai across eight offers, seats, campaign credits, prediction limits and US contract conditions.
factual.intro: Choose the campaign job before the subscription: brand-controlled writing, repeatable GTM content workflows, predictive copy iteration or visual ad production. These four supplier families overlap in content production but expose different output and usage limits. A predicted performance number is not an observed conversion lift, and a product-level workflow description does not prove that every paid tier includes it. factual.heading: AI image tools for US creative teams
factual.description: Compare Adobe Firefly, Canva, Ideogram and Midjourney across eight image-creation offers, private generation, US prices and commercial-use limits.
factual.intro: Choose an image workflow before choosing a model. A campaign concept, an editable brand layout and a confidential product visualization require different controls even when all begin with a text prompt. These four independent supplier families cover generation and editing, but their subscription units, collaboration and publication defaults differ. The comparison keeps eight named offers separate and does not assign an image-quality winner from a feature checklist.
factual.localHeading: US prices, tax and the right commercial offer
factual.localNote: Adobe’s explicit US locale lists Firefly Standard at USD 9.99 and Pro at USD 19.99 per month; the plain page returned CHF, which is not used here. Canva lists USD 144 and 250 per person annually for Pro and Business, with applicable US sales tax added according to billing address. Ideogram explicitly prices in USD before tax. Midjourney accepts USD and requires Pro or Mega when a company exceeds USD 1 million in gross annual revenue. A commercial-use permission does not resolve every third-party right or establish exclusive copyright.
factual.checklistHeading: Define the deliverable and privacy requirement first
factual.costNote: Count paid seats, generated attempts, edits, upscales, model-specific consumption and occasional extra credits. Compare an annual commitment with another annual commitment. Relax queues, unlimited standard features and paid extra credits describe different limits; none proves unlimited use of every model.

comparison.title: Ideogram vs Midjourney: private images, credits and commercial tiers
comparison.description: Compare Ideogram Plus/Pro with Midjourney Standard/Pro using documented privacy, usage and US commercial-offer boundaries.
comparison.intro: Both create images, but a credit wallet and a GPU-time subscription do not buy the same workload. Choose the privacy and commercial-use route before comparing the monthly price.

choices.heading: Consider Ideogram for private generation and predictable tier boundaries
choices.text: Plus includes private generation and quality export; Pro adds batch generation. Monthly credits expire and additional credit purchases do not change the tier. Price the actual operations rather than treating every generated image as one identical credit.

choices.heading: Consider Midjourney for a GPU-time and queue workflow
choices.text: Standard and Pro provide Relax image generation, while Pro adds Stealth and more Fast capacity. The commercial revenue threshold can rule out Standard even before performance is considered. A private subscription does not make a public Discord post confidential.

factual.name: AI data analysis and reporting
factual.heading: AI data-analysis tools for US teams
factual.description: Compare Julius, Bricks, Sourcetable and Better Analyst across eight offers, calculation inspection, report delivery, data controls and billing uncertainty.
factual.intro: An attractive chart is not evidence that the calculation is correct. Start with a known dataset, a repeatable question and a defined recipient. These tools overlap in analysis and reporting but differ in compute, message allowances, recurring tasks and client delivery. Product-wide connectors are separated from entitlements established for each selected plan. Unknown invoice details and contradictory team allowances remain visible rather than becoming a cheapest-product ranking.
factual.localHeading: US procurement and data handling are separate decisions
factual.localNote: Julius explicitly lists USD 20 and 45 monthly for Plus and Pro; its privacy notice requests that users do not upload sensitive personal data. Bricks publishes a US company agreement but its dollar currency and conflicting seat descriptions remain unresolved. Sourcetable’s FAQ documents US ACH and USD support while also showing inconsistent legacy prices. Better Analyst is supplied by Datasetmatch LLC and uses Stripe checkout; the exact public dollar currency and tax remain unverified. None of these observations establishes suitability for regulated data.
factual.checklistHeading: Inspect the calculation, recipient and usage meter
factual.costNote: Budget the exact seats, AI messages, bulk-processing credits, compute and embedded-client use. Better Analyst’s paid chat is separate from bulk AI credits and embedded messages. A large message allowance does not remove file, refresh or compute limits.

factual.name: General AI assistants
factual.heading: General AI assistant plans for US users
factual.description: Compare ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Mistral Vibe across eight personal or team offers, US access, tool limits, contracts and unresolved prices.
factual.intro: A general assistant can help with research, drafts and files, but a personal subscription is not automatically a company workspace or an API budget. This comparison separates eight named offers from four supplier families. It records documented tool boundaries and US availability without inventing an accuracy score. Choose the recurring work, account controls and exact allowance first; model names and headline message claims can change more quickly than the underlying workflow.
factual.localHeading: US access does not remove account and contract conditions
factual.localNote: ChatGPT and Claude explicitly list the United States as supported. ChatGPT Plus and Pro 100 are monthly personal offers, and Claude’s help page explicitly quotes the US Pro price. Claude Max’s displayed dollar amount remains a currency-confirmation gap in this packet. Google’s United States plan page exposes benefits but no numeric prices; certain Gmail and Photos functions are specifically US-only and still have account conditions. Mistral’s retrieved France/education selector does not establish a US tariff; outside-EEA consumer and commercial agreements are separate.
factual.checklistHeading: Compare the work and permission boundary
factual.costNote: Separate subscription allowances, purchased credits, API consumption and third-party services. ChatGPT’s API is billed separately. Claude Pro does not include Console usage; Max’s advertised credit benefit has its own eligibility and renewal conditions. Google family sharing is not enterprise administration.

comparison.title: ChatGPT vs Claude: personal subscriptions, usage windows and API boundaries
comparison.description: Compare ChatGPT Plus/Pro 100 and Claude Pro/Max without inheriting enterprise controls or treating allowances as measured output quality.
comparison.intro: Choose an assistant by the recurring task and exact account permissions. These personal subscriptions have different usage windows and API relationships; none is a guarantee that a research answer or generated document is correct.

choices.heading: Consider ChatGPT for a mixed personal workflow
choices.text: Plus and Pro 100 offer different model and tool allowances. API usage is separate, connected tools can draw from the same approved allowance, and Ultrafast is not included in Pro 100. Inspect the actual account rather than assuming every advertised option has rolled out.

choices.heading: Consider Claude for its document and connected-tool workflow
choices.text: Pro uses five-hour and weekly limits, while Max expands usage. The personal plans are not a shared enterprise workspace. Pro API consumption is separate; the Max credit benefit should be checked for eligibility and expiry before it enters a budget.
