comparisons.title: Brevo vs GetResponse: match the audience, sends and automation before comparing cost
comparisons.summary: Compare contact counting, sending volume and automation scope before choosing an email platform. This US buying brief explains the questions to put to each supplier without inventing an equivalent price or a universal winner.
comparisons.decision: Start with Brevo when you want to evaluate a configured sending allowance alongside contact storage. Start with GetResponse when you want to evaluate its list-size billing and the workflow scope of its named plans. Both need the same real audience and campaign scenario before a cost comparison is meaningful.

rows.label: Buying unit
rows.left: Selected monthly email tier also sets contact storage limits.
rows.right: Billing considers peak active subscribers and contacts added during the month.

rows.label: Automation scope
rows.left: The reviewed Standard plan lists automation for unlimited contacts; confirm the selected offer and other usage limits.
rows.right: Starter lists one custom workflow; Marketer lists unlimited workflows.

rows.label: What to inspect
rows.left: Contact-tier thresholds, monthly sends, extra seats and required add-ons.
rows.right: List structure, repeated addresses across lists, contact growth and the required plan.

rows.label: US budget
rows.left: Obtain the actual checkout currency, applicable tax basis, billing term and complete configuration.
rows.right: Obtain the actual checkout currency, applicable tax basis, billing term and complete configuration.

sections.heading: Count the same audience in both offers
sections.body: Brevo's plan documentation links its sending tiers to contact storage. GetResponse's billing guidance counts an address on multiple lists separately and describes charges based on peak active subscribers and contacts added during the month. A single number labelled contacts is therefore not a sufficient budget specification.
bullets: Record your unique audience, list memberships, monthly additions and expected sends.
Ask each supplier how that exact inventory is counted, including a month when you import or reorganise contacts.

sections.heading: Choose the workflow before the tier
sections.body: The reviewed Brevo Standard description includes automation for unlimited contacts. GetResponse's pricing page distinguishes Starter's single custom workflow from Marketer's unlimited workflows. These statements do not establish that every action, channel or integration needed by your business is included.
bullets: Draw one welcome or purchase-triggered journey, including a stop condition.
Confirm the plan covering each event, segment and action before comparing the final quote.

sections.heading: Use a small, observable rehearsal
sections.body: Run the same fictional customer journey in each trial. Add a test contact, change a relevant attribute, trigger the next step and then withdraw the contact from the journey. Record what occurred and what required manual intervention. This is our suggested evaluation method, not a report of hands-on product testing.
bullets: Check the event history and why a contact did or did not continue.
Inspect a sample export and the handling of suppression records before planning a migration.

sections.heading: Request a complete US proposal
sections.body: Ask for the ordinary ongoing charge, billing period, currency and applicable tax treatment for your organisation. Add the users, channels and integrations actually required. Keep quote-only items unresolved until confirmed; do not convert a displayed international starting price into an assumed USD total.
bullets: Model an ordinary month and a busier month using the same assumptions.
Separate temporary discounts from renewal terms and clarify what triggers a higher tier.

limitations: Documentary comparison of the linked public sources checked on 13 November 2026; no hands-on trial, deliverability measurement or final editorial rating.
Specific US prices, supplier commitments and compatibility with your existing integrations still require confirmation.
Existing product-profile assessments have their own dates and scope; this article does not refresh every catalogue assessment.

comparisons.decision: Put ClickUp on the shortlist when you want to evaluate a workspace bringing tasks and documents together. Put monday work management on the shortlist when configurable boards are central to your proposed process. Choose between them using the same handoff, reporting and guest-access rehearsal, then confirm the required tier.

rows.left: Automation allowances and Brain² access or credits differ by tier.

rows.left: Confirm paid users, guest permissions, billing term, currency and extra usage.
rows.right: Confirm paid seats, seat minimums, guest permissions, billing term and extra usage.

sections.heading: Use the current plan names
sections.body: ClickUp's reviewed pricing page now describes Core, Business, Enterprise and MAX alongside Free Forever. Older comparisons using different plan names or assuming every AI capability is a separate add-on may no longer describe the offer. monday's work management pricing also combines seat plans with differing AI and automation allowances.
bullets: Save the exact offer and billing configuration used for the trial.
Ask whether a trial feature remains available on the intended paid plan.

sections.heading: Rehearse a changed deadline
sections.body: Create a small project with an owner, a contributor and a reviewer. Delay an input, return one item for revision and ask a colleague to find the next action. Observe whether the process remains understandable without rebuilding it in a second tracker. These are proposed acceptance checks, not claims that either product passed a test.
bullets: Distinguish automatic date changes from warnings and manual updates.
Record the context carried from the contributor to the reviewer.

sections.heading: Inspect the roles behind the seat count
sections.body: The ClickUp page distinguishes guest permissions and higher-tier governance features. monday distinguishes free viewers from other access arrangements. A team size alone does not tell you which people can do the work required; verify what an occasional reviewer, external collaborator and administrator can access on your selected tier.
bullets: Try the actual role rather than using an administrator for every demonstration.
Include the intended number of paid people and any purchase minimums in the proposal.

sections.heading: Keep automation and AI in the budget
sections.body: Both current pricing pages differentiate usage by tier. Determine which repetitive actions you will run, how often they occur and which AI capabilities matter. Have the supplier explain the charging unit and what happens at the allowance boundary. A credit, an action and a seat should not be treated as interchangeable units.
bullets: Request an ordinary-month estimate and a busier-month estimate.
Confirm US billing currency, applicable tax treatment, renewal terms and any usage charges before committing.

limitations: Official pricing-page research checked on 13 November 2026; no hands-on trial or final editorial rating.

comparisons.title: Power BI vs Tableau: compare the reporting audience before the licence price
comparisons.summary: Compare author and viewer access, deployment choices and AI prerequisites before judging a dashboard platform by its entry price. Use a shared dataset and a realistic audience to shape the decision.
comparisons.decision: Start a Power BI evaluation by mapping report authors, recipients and any required Fabric capacity. Start a Tableau evaluation by choosing the deployment and edition, then the Creator, Explorer and Viewer mix. The useful shortlist is the one whose sharing and administration model fits your actual audience.

rows.label: Licensing question
rows.left: Distinguish free creation, Pro or Premium Per User access, and capacity arrangements.
rows.right: Distinguish the selected edition, deployment and Creator, Explorer or Viewer roles.

rows.label: Deployment
rows.left: Check the Power BI service and any Fabric capacity required for your use case.
rows.right: Separate Tableau Cloud, Server and Next rather than treating them as one offer.

rows.label: AI prerequisite
rows.left: Copilot needs eligible organisational capacity; Pro or PPU alone is insufficient.
rows.right: Confirm the edition and capabilities in the proposal; Tableau Cloud+ and bundle offers have different scope.

rows.label: Acceptance test
rows.left: Open the report as each intended audience role and verify permitted data and refresh behaviour.
rows.right: Open the report as each intended audience role and verify permitted data and refresh behaviour.

sections.heading: Price the audience, not one author
sections.body: Power BI's public offer separates free report creation, Pro and Premium Per User access, and capacity options. Tableau offers different deployment and edition choices, with Creator, Explorer and Viewer roles; its pricing page states that a deployment needs at least one Creator. Ask for the configuration matching your authors and recipients before comparing a per-user headline.
bullets: List authors, internal readers and any external recipients separately.
Ask which licence each role needs for the exact sharing arrangement.

sections.heading: Treat AI eligibility as a separate check
sections.body: Microsoft's Copilot documentation requires eligible paid organisational capacity and relevant administrative and regional settings; Pro or Premium Per User alone is insufficient. Tableau's pricing distinguishes editions and AI-related scope. Do not infer that a familiar product name or an entry licence includes the AI experience shown in a demonstration.
bullets: Name the specific AI experience and have the supplier identify its prerequisites.
Test answers against known business definitions before using them in a decision.

sections.heading: Test one report with two audience roles
sections.body: Use a non-sensitive sample dataset with a definition of the metric, a known expected result and two different viewer roles. Ask each reviewer to open the report, apply a filter and explain the number. Then verify that each role sees only its permitted records. This is an editorial test plan, not certification of either supplier's configuration.
bullets: Test the recipient experience separately from the author's workspace.
Record the source timestamp and what happens when a refresh is delayed.

sections.heading: Include the work around the dashboard
sections.body: Budget for the complete proposal: users, capacity or hosting, the chosen edition, data preparation and ongoing ownership. Confirm the actual US currency, billing period and applicable tax basis rather than treating an international starting rate as a local quote. Record who maintains the data model and responds when a source changes.
bullets: Request one cost model for the initial audience and another for expected growth.
Keep unanswered sharing, regional and administrative requirements visible until they are resolved.

limitations: Documentary research checked on 13 November 2026; no hands-on trial, performance benchmark or final editorial rating.
No universal cheapest configuration is claimed. US checkout terms, deployment details and actual AI eligibility require confirmation.
Existing product scores and assessments have separate dates and scope; publication of this article does not revalidate them.

/partners/.html:
Represent a software supplier? Ask our editorial team to assess your product for the relevant System Compare country editions and categories.

Start with a free application

This program is for businesses. Applying is free and creates no listing or payment obligation. Our team manually checks eligibility before proposing a service.

Apply for supplier onboarding ↗

Prefer email? Write to partnerships@system-compare.com.

How onboarding works

  1. Free application: identify your company, product, official website and requested markets.
  2. Eligibility review: our team manually checks whether the product is suitable for further assessment. This is not approval for a published listing.
  3. Private continuation: after eligibility approval, our team sends or arranges a personal continuation link to the verified application email. There you can review the proposed research scope, final fee and full commercial terms before deciding whether to proceed. Keep your application reference; invitation delivery is a separate step after approval.
  4. Research and editorial review: if you choose the agreed paid service, we research public official sources, record feature and plan evidence, and check the draft.
  5. Publication decision: the editorial team decides eligibility, category placement and publication under the same comparison methodology.

Three types of request

You can apply to add a supplier to an existing category, propose a new category together with your supplier, or request a separately agreed rescan of an existing listing. A category proposal must identify at least five distinct companies and their official websites so our team can assess whether a meaningful comparison is possible.

An included review is scheduled six calendar months after a completed listing review. This is not a subscription or automatic renewal charge. Factual corrections remain free; a separate rescan is agreed only when it is additional work outside an included review.

Before you commit to a service

The initial application and eligibility review do not create a payment obligation. If your application is eligible, any proposed paid research and onboarding service will be explained in the private continuation before you agree: products and country editions included, work and deliverable, expected delivery period, final price, applicable taxes, cancellation and refund terms, and any later updates.

The final price in a current service proposal includes applicable taxes, without a separate tax breakdown. Supplier scan and analysis are completed within 3 calendar weeks after both verified payment and receipt of the required onboarding information. Payments are non-refundable, except where applicable law or applicable payment-provider protections require otherwise. Nothing in these terms limits mandatory statutory rights.

You can decide whether to proceed after reviewing those details. Applying does not purchase a service, create a subscription or guarantee a permanent or worldwide listing.

Terms for new supplier onboarding

For this new program, published product features, prices and plan comparisons are researched from the supplier’s publicly accessible official website and documentation. We record sources and review dates. Application details identify the business, verify authority and administer the request; private or unsupported product claims are not treated as verified editorial evidence.

Suppliers may point us to relevant public official URLs and request correction of factual errors. Information we cannot verify stays marked as unknown. /methodology/.title: How our comparisons work
/methodology/.description: One documented-fit score using four weighted groups, official evidence and an 80% checked-weight gate.
/methodology/.html:
Each vendor in a category is assessed against the same checklist. The score describes documented support for that checklist, not product quality, customer satisfaction or a hands-on performance test.

Four groups

  • Core capabilities: 45. The category’s main job, plus generic security, compliance, reliability and support.
  • Integrations: 20. Exchange of records, events or identity with other systems: APIs, webhooks, native connectors, import/export and SSO.
  • Local suitability: 20. Explicit US language, tax, payroll, legal, payment, data-residency or local-system requirements.
  • AI: 15. AI and machine-learning capabilities, including their evidence and action controls. Main AI functions are core in categories whose main job is AI.

Country-specific requirements take precedence. AI takes precedence over integrations, except the main AI job in an AI category. Every item belongs to one group. A group with no active items is omitted and the remaining group weights are normalized to 100. Within each active group, items share its weight equally. Commercial terms remain core and are flagged for review.

How each item contributes

  • Supported: official documentation establishes the complete defined capability; value 1.
  • Limited or paid add-on: documented partial capability or a separate paid add-on; value 0.5.
  • Not supported: official documentation explicitly establishes absence; value 0.
  • Not verified: no qualifying official source and checked date; value 0 and excluded from checked coverage. A supplier-confirmed statement alone earns no points.

A capability available only on a higher plan can receive full credit in a product-wide comparison when that plan is named. A named-plan comparison uses only evidence for that plan. Product-wide evidence is never copied into an unresearched plan.

The research gate and equal treatment

A score is shown only when at least 80% of the active checklist weight has a checked status, including documented absence. Otherwise the vendor shows Score pending, the number checked and the checked weight. Unverified is not a claim that a capability is absent.

A deep check contributes points only after every listed vendor in that category has a checked result. Until then it remains visible, labeled inactive, and has no weight for any vendor. This prevents a deeper examination of one vendor from changing its position before its competitors have received the same examination.

One score and one ordering rule

The published score is rounded once to a whole number, with half values rounded away from zero. Scored vendors appear before pending vendors. Products sharing a displayed score are ordered by the unrounded score, then counted capability coverage, then the fully documented item count, then name. Pending vendors are ordered by name. Every vendor sharing the highest positive displayed score receives the Recommended label.

Coverage describes research completeness. The documented-item count includes active supported and partially supported items; the checked count also includes documented absence. Neither is a customer rating. The date beside a score comes from the underlying evidence and is not changed by a methodology release.

Controls and scope

Category filters change which checklist rows you see. Plan selection changes the evidence scope. Neither changes the published four-group weights. There is no alternative score with AI removed. The same price, source and affiliate-disclosure rules apply to every vendor.

Homepage selection

The featured homepage products use CRM’s published score order. Category previews follow catalogue category order, show the top two scored vendors, and disclose every tied leader. A later preview is skipped if one of its tied leaders already appears as a leader in an earlier preview. Categories need at least two scored products. No vendor pays for placement.

Evidence, prices and corrections

Research uses official product, help, pricing and developer documentation. Proposed demo questions are tasks for a buyer to test, not claims that our team completed a product trial. Price, billing unit, taxes, plan restrictions and source dates remain attached to the underlying research. Send corrections with the exact product, plan, checklist item and official source to support@system-compare.com.

Method change, 13 November 2026: one score per vendor from four weighted groups; no ranges; scores shown after 80% of the checklist weight is checked. All scores were recalculated. Methodology version 4.0. This method date does not advance any product or price-check date.

Scoped research refreshes

A public-source pricing and plan review does not re-score every capability. Individual evidence dates remain visible. See recent checks and open questions and editorial responsibility.

Information used to provide the site

Filters and calculations are processed in your browser. If you choose to save a shortlist, it is stored in this browser's local storage, not in a user account. You can erase it with the Privacy choices control or your browser settings.

Analytics and advertising

Google Analytics 4 is optional and loads only after you select Allow analytics. Rejecting has no effect on access to the website. With permission, Google processes page visits, approximate location, browser/device information and events such as opening comparisons, adding a product to a shortlist, following a vendor link or submitting a cost calculation. We do not send form contents, calculator amounts, search terms or URL query strings to Analytics. Google receives technical connection information, including your IP address, to process requests. Advertising features and Google signals are disabled. We do not install advertising pixels, use newsletter forms or transfer your shortlist to vendors. Hosting providers may use necessary security or authentication storage.

Your analytics preference is stored locally for 180 days. Analytics cookies named _ga and _ga_* are configured for a lifetime of up to 12 months; browser settings may shorten this. Event and user-level Analytics data is retained for two months; standard aggregated reports are not subject to that setting. Open Cookie settings or Privacy choices to withdraw permission at any time. Withdrawal disables future collection, removes this site’s Analytics cookies and reloads the page when needed; it does not erase previously collected data. See Google’s privacy policy.

When you contact us or visit a vendor

Email links open your own email application. If you send a message, we receive its contents and your contact details to respond and handle the request. Do not send payment details, identity documents, health information or account passwords. External links lead to services with their own privacy notices. Sharing, retention and international processing

Technical providers process data as needed to run the service. We may disclose information when required by applicable law or to protect the service. This release does not sell personal information or share it for cross-context behavioral advertising. Processing can occur outside your state or country, including Israel, the United States (Google Analytics) and hosting-provider locations. Where applicable, international transfers are subject to the providers’ contractual safeguards. We retain correspondence only while needed to address the request, maintain necessary business records or meet legal obligations; infrastructure logs follow provider retention settings.

Your requests

Depending on your location and applicable law, you may have rights to access, correct, delete or obtain a copy of personal information, object to certain processing, or appeal a decision. Contact us using the email above with the request and enough information to identify the relevant interaction. We may verify your identity using information proportionate to the request. You may use an authorized agent where applicable. We will not penalize you for exercising an applicable privacy right.

A detected Global Privacy Control signal disables optional Analytics, including a previously saved opt-in. Do Not Track does not enable any tracking: our consent requirement still applies. We do not sell personal information or share it for cross-context behavioral advertising. California residents can read the California Attorney General's privacy rights guidance.
